## G218. A genuine cofactor average with a fixed zero detector

Let R mean positive integers or nonzero integral ideals of K=Q(omega).
Write q_a=a or N(a). Fix a finite prime set S, tau>0 and one ordinary
Dirichlet character eta or finite-order trivial-infinity Hecke character.
All natural zero primes of the PRESENTED character remain. For the sextic
application S contains the primes above6. Let Q be a finite radical
coprime to S and put

    g(v)=(2*pi*tau)^(-1/2) exp(-v^2/(2tau)),
    U_Q(x)=sum_a mu_R(a)eta(a)1_((a,SQ)=1)g(log(q_a/x)),
    U=U_1.                                                (218.1)

These are complete infinite sums. Norm-Euclidean division in the
triangular lattice makes every Eisenstein ideal principal. The covolume
sqrt(3)/2 and six units give A_K(T)=kappa T+O(sqrt T),
kappa=pi/(3sqrt3); A_Z(T)=T+O(1). The first count remains valid at0<T<1
because the count is zero and T<=sqrt T. In particular A_R(T)<<T for
T>=1, |U_Q(x)|<<x uniformly in Q, and the small-x Gaussian tail is smaller
than every fixed power. No Moebius cancellation is used in these bounds.

Take the exact finite sets

    Fset={f squarefree:F<q_f<=2F,(f,S)=1},
    Eset={e:q_e<=E,(e,S)=1},
    P_FE(x)=(N_F N_E)^(-1)sum_(f,e)U_rad(fe)(x).             (218.2)

Shared f,e primes and every e valuation are allowed. The counts N_F,N_E
are their actual cardinalities, comparable to F,E once the fixed-S
threshold is passed. Freeze F,E throughout each shell. For a radical Q,
write h(Q)=prod_(p|Q)(1-q_p^-1), D(Q)=prod_(p|Q)(1+q_p^-1)^-1 and
S_a(Q)=sum_(d|Q)q_d^-a. Inclusion-exclusion followed by
mu^2(n)=sum_(r^2|n)mu(r) gives, uniformly in Q and for T>=1,

    A_Q^sf(T)=kappa T D(Q)/zeta_K(2)
                  +O(sqrt T log(2T)S_1/2(Q))             [K],
    A_Q^sf(T)=T D(Q)/zeta(2)+O(sqrt T d(Q))               [Z]. (218.3)

Indeed the lattice errors sum to sqrt T S_1/2(Q)sum_(q_r<=sqrt T)q_r^-1;
the omitted main tail is O(sqrt T). The integer floor errors are at most
sqrt T d(Q). The main coefficient uses h(Q)prod_(p|Q)(1-q_p^-2)^-1=D(Q).
There is no Q<=T restriction. The T>=1 qualification corrects the raw
author's tiny-T log(2T) notation; its uses at F,E are unaffected.

The squarefree-f and unrestricted-e avoidance probabilities have main
terms A(a)=prod_(p|a,p notin S)q_p/(q_p+1) and
B(a)=prod_(p|a,p notin S)(q_p-1)/q_p. Division by the EXACT sample counts
retains the same error order. Their errors add when multiplying, since
all four probabilities/main terms lie in[0,1]. Define the ONE fixed field

    W_w(x)=sum_a mu_R(a)eta(a)1_((a,S)=1)w(a)g(log(q_a/x)),
    w_p=(q_p-1)/(q_p+1).                                  (218.4)

Then, uniformly for x>0 and sufficiently large F,E,

    |P_FE-W_w| << x log(2F)(F^-1/2+E^-1/2)                [K],
    |P_FE-W_w| << x(1+log(2+x))(F^-1/2+E^-1)              [Z]. (218.5)

Both source tails are included: sum_(q_a<=T)S_1/2(rad a)<<T follows by
divisor summation and sum_d q_d^-3/2<infinity; the integer analogue is
sum_(n<=T)d(rad n)<<T log(2T). Partial summation against the entire
Gaussian gives(218.5). For x<1, writing L=log(1/x) separates a factor
exp(-L^2/(2tau)), which dominates every required fixed power.

The boundary cases are DIFFERENT fixed sources, not substitutions into
the two-sided limiting density. With e=1, let P_F^sf=N_F^-1 sum_f U_f;
its weight is A_p=q_p/(q_p+1) and its sole error is the F term above.
With f=1 and an unrestricted e average the weight is1-q_p^-1 and its
sole error is the E term. This preserves the unit cofactor explicitly.

For any of these three weights w_p=1-delta_p, delta_p is respectively
2/(q_p+1),1/(q_p+1),1/q_p. On Re s>1, absolute Fubini gives

    Mellin W_w(s)=exp(tau*s^2/2)H_w(s)/L^S(s,eta),
    H_w=prod_(p notin S)(1-w_p z_p)/(1-z_p),
    z_p=eta(p)q_p^-s.                                     (218.6)

Both H_w and its inverse have coefficient series in every l1_sigma,
sigma>0. Their local expansions are

    H_p=1+delta_p sum_(j>=1)z_p^j,
    H_p^-1=1-delta_p sum_(j>=1)w_p^(j-1)z_p^j.

The nonconstant absolute mass is O_sigma(q_p^(-1-sigma)); all local
denominators/numerators are nonzero on that half-plane. The normally
convergent inverse proves global nonvanishing. Eta(p)=0 contributes1.
The full Gaussian convolution identities W_w=h*U and U=h_inv*W_w use
V(x/q_d), with cost sum_d|h(d)|q_d^-sigma in the norm

    ||V||_(sigma,p)=sup_(X>0)X^-sigma||V||_(Lp([X,2X],dx/x)), p=1,2.

Formation is justified at sigma=1 before an unproved smaller exponent is
used. The small shifted scales have already been paid. Thus these FIXED
fields have equal every-epsilon shell exponent classes for gamma>0.

For gamma=1-c in(0,1), an every-epsilon complete shell L1 bound
||P_FE||_1<<X^(gamma+epsilon), with F=X^v,E=X^r fixed across the shell,
returns to W_w when v>=2c and r>=2c over K, or v>=2c and r>=c over Z.
For f-only, v>=2c suffices in both rings. Equality allows the displayed
logarithms through the every-epsilon convention. First pass to the fixed
field, then Mellin transform. Large-shell dyadic summation and the left
Gaussian tail prove normal convergence of all fixed derivatives on
Re s>gamma. The continued identity L^S Mellin W_w=exp(tau*s^2/2)H_w
excludes every zero there; the possible principal pole at1 is preserved.
Finite omitted Euler factors only have zeros on Re s=0.

For an ordinary-family conclusion gamma must be common to every positive
modulus/character, while constants and onsets may depend on the fixed
member. The ideal-field version covers only the stated Hecke family and
does not prove the ordinary premise. No moving cutoff is assigned a fixed
Mellin transform. All these returns need the still-OPEN signed L1 bound.

## G219. Actual principal channels and the cheapest generic price

Use the fixed primary representatives and symbol of
[[research revision] G212-G214](../[research revision]/sieve-layer-integration.md). On all good ideals,
with original zero extension,

    chi_a(f)^4 chi_a(f^2 e^6)=1_((a,fe)=1).                (219.1)

At a shared prime the left side remains zero; on coprime inputs its total
symbol exponent is divisible by6. Global primary multiplicativity keeps
the unit. This is not an arbitrary insertion of labels into an old source.

For X=Z^N,F=Z^V,E=Z^R form the genuinely NEW coefficient family

    T_fk(x)=X^-1/2 sum_a mu_K(a)eta(a)1_((a,S)=1)
                  chi_a(k)chi_a(f)^4 g(log(q_a/x)).       (219.2)

The non-character coefficients/profile are independent of f,k. They are
not canonical Gauss coefficients, the old physical numerator, or a PR26
source. On k=f^2e^6, T_fk=X^-1/2 U_rad(fe). For fixed f the map e->k is
injective, q_k<=4F^2E^6, and the selected PAIR count is exactly N_F N_E.
Thus, with M=2V+6R,

    B_FE=(N_F N_E)^(-1)sum_(f,e)||U_rad(fe)||_2^2,
    J=F^-1 sum_f sum_(q_k<=4Z^M)||T_fk||_2^2,
    B_FE <= C_S X E^-1 J.                               (219.3)

There is no extra division by F or by the full row count. All row
repetitions remain. Gaussian annuli have polynomial derivative factors
times exp(-c j^2); all length prices grow at most exponentially in|j|.
Minkowski sums the complete profile, including unit/short-source annuli.

Conditional on [research revision]'s NAMED sixth-order and squarefree cubic sieve inputs,
its arbitrary fixed-column proof applies here and gives J<<Z^(Emix+eps),

    Emix(M,N,V)=sup_(0<=t<=M){(M-t)/6+min(C(t,N),t+L)},
    C(t,N)=max(t,N,5t/6+N/3,t/3+5N/6),
    L=max(0,N-V,(2N-V)/3).                              (219.4)

No new external admission or Moebius-specific sieve estimate is asserted.
In particular k=f^2 cannot be substituted BEFORE using a free f-average.
The t=V member gives Emix>=N+(M-V)/6 and hence the recovered upper-bound
PRICE N+Emix-R>=2N+V/6. It cannot certify gamma<1.

For fixed N,V, subtracting R leaves exactly

    Emix(2V+6R,N,V)-R
      =sup_(0<=t<=2V+6R){(2V-t)/6+min(C(t,N),t+L)}.       (219.5)

Only the domain grows with R, so extra e repetitions cannot improve this
recovered certificate. The f-only detector legitimately uses e=1, M=2V,
weight A_p and B_F^sf<=C X J. At N=1 the FULL envelope is

    Emix(2v,1,v)=1+v/6           for0<=v<=1/3,
                 5/6+2v/3       for1/3<=v<=1/2,
                 1/3+5v/3       for1/2<=v<=1,
                 2v            forv>=1.                (219.6)

For v<=1/2, L=1-v: the only extra maximum is t=v with value1+v/6;
compare it with the endpoint C(2v,1). Their crossing is v=1/3. For
v>=1/2 the endpoint gives the remaining two pieces. All pieces increase,
so the least field-admissible choice is v=2c. Its energy price is2+c/3
for c<=1/6, or11/6+4c/3 for1/6<=c<=1/4.

| Target c | Required energy | f-only certificate | Unpaid difference |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
|.12|1.76|2.04|.28|
|conditional .1251459636|1.7497080728|2.0417153212|.2920072484|
|1/6|5/3|37/18|7/18|
|1/4|3/2|13/6|2/3|

The e-only detector has price1+max(5r,1,4r+1/3,r+5/6), r>=2c over K.
It is worse at the tabulated targets, but can be cheaper for sufficiently
small c. F-only is optimal within the squarefree-label branch, not among
all possible detector architectures. These are certificate prices, not
lower bounds on the actual signed source.

A FIXED positive counterexample rejects coefficient-uniform power gains:
replace mu_K(a) by mu_K(a)^2 conjugate(eta(a)). For the lower count use
S+=S union ALL natural-zero primes of the presented character. On this
subset the product with eta is mu_K(a)^2, with no discarded negative term.
For q_Q<=X^A, (218.3), S_1/2(Q)<<q_Q^delta and D(Q)>>q_Q^-delta show
uniformly that there are >>X^(1-eps) good squarefree a in(X,2X]. Choose
delta so the square-root error is below the positive main term. The
Gaussian is bounded below on q_a,x in[X,2X]; consequently the positive
source has B_FE>=X^(2-o(1)) and J>=Z^(N+R-o(1)). The signed average is
also positive. This array satisfies the generic column contract, but is
not actual mu or canonical Gauss data. It rules out only a gain asserted
uniformly for that coefficient class.

statement:
## G220. Complete finite covariance and the limiting-bank alternative

For a fixed finite Q coprime to S, coefficientwise Euler factors give

    U_Q(x)=sum_(d Q-smooth)eta(d)U(x/q_d),
    U(x)=sum_(d|Q)mu(d)eta(d)U_Q(x/q_d).                   (220.1)

Both are complete absolutely formed Gaussian identities. For every
sigma,delta>0, prod_(p|Q)(1-q_p^-sigma)^-1<<q_Q^delta: split off finitely
many small primes and bound each remaining factor by q_p^delta. Thus
an all-shell exponent gamma>0 for U implies the same exponent uniformly
for polynomial-size Q, with arbitrarily small extra loss and small
shifted scales retained. Conversely, Jensen, (218.5) and the fixed Euler
inverse recover U from a complete positive-bank L2 bound, when the FIELD
error gate is paid. Hence those bank and U shell-L2 exponent classes are
equivalent. This does not identify L1 with L2.

For f-only let p_F(d)=N_F^-1#{f in Fset:(f,d)=1},
K_X(a,b)=integral_X^(2X)g(log(q_a/x))g(log(q_b/x))dx/x and
c_a=mu_R(a)eta(a)1_((a,S)=1). The exact finite bank is

    B_F^sf=sum_(a,b)c_a conjugate(c_b)K_X(a,b)p_F(rad(ab)). (220.2)

The squared averaged FIELD instead has kernel p_F(a)p_F(b). These
kernels differ by the entire label covariance. No independent-prime
model is used at finite F. On the actual squarefree coefficient support,

    A(rad(ab))=A(a)A(b)sum_(d|gcd(a,b))q_d^-1.

Therefore the limiting bank has the exact positive feature expansion

    B_infty(X)=sum_(d squarefree,(d,S)=1)q_d^-1 ||V_d||_2^2,
    V_d(x)=sum_(d|a)c_a A(a)g(log(q_a/x)).                (220.3)

The d=1 term is ||W_A||_2^2, and all other terms are the full limiting
label variance. Absolute Gaussian majorants justify every rearrangement:
after the divisor expansion the absolute factor is A(rad(ab))<=1.

Replacing the FINITE kernel by this limit costs

    |B_F^sf-B_infty| << X^2 F^-1/2 log(2F)              [K],
    |B_F^sf-B_infty| << X^2 F^-1/2(1+log(2+X))^2        [Z]. (220.4)

Indeed the avoidance-probability error at rad(ab) is bounded by the
product of its separate divisor majorants, and each Gaussian sum is
O(x), or O(x log(2+x)) over Z. Thus this ENERGY replacement needs v>=4c
at exponent2-2c, whereas the FIELD comparison only needs v>=2c. Keeping
(220.2) exact avoids this extra approximation.

There is also a fully paid DIRECT limiting-bank return. If W_A has an
all-shell L2 exponent sigma>0, remove the primes of d from its weighted
Euler product. The inverse factors are(1-A_p eta(p)q_p^-s)^-1, whose
l1_sigma cost is at most C_(sigma,delta)q_d^delta. For squarefree d,

    V_d(x)=mu(d)eta(d)A(d)W_(A,d)(x/q_d).

Hence for any0<delta<sigma,

    B_infty(X) <= C ||W_A||_(sigma,2)^2 X^(2sigma)
                    sum_d q_d^(-1-2sigma+2delta).        (220.5)

The sum converges by A_R(T)<<T, and every d and small shifted scale is
included. Conversely B_infty>=||W_A||_2^2, followed by the fixed inverse
in G218. Thus B_infty and U have the same every-epsilon L2 exponent class
for gamma>0. Estimating B_infty directly would need no finite-F limit
error, but its ENTIRE infinite hole family must then be paid. This
corollary does not permit substituting a finite-bank bound without(220.4),
and supplies no arithmetic saving. It leaves the exact signed finite
field/Gram and the direct limiting bank as distinct lawful targets.
title: G220. Complete finite covariance and the limiting-bank alternative

## G221. The user's quaternion identity on the actual Jordan source

Retain G215-G216's fixed ordinary chi, parity-matched r>=2, fixed m,
complete filtered error E_m and lambda=2^(r+1). Put A_X=E_m(X),
B_X=E_m(X/2). In the user's convention jz=conjugate(z)j,

    (A_X+B_X j)(1+lambda j)=Phi(X)+Psi(X)j,
    Phi=A_X-lambda B_X, Psi=lambda A_X+B_X,
    |Phi|^2+|Psi|^2=(1+lambda^2)(|A_X|^2+|B_X|^2).         (221.1)

The multiplier coefficients are real, so this applies to complex chi
without a conjugation or chi(2) error, including2|q. The companion source
is explicit: if E_m=sum mu(n)chi(n)H(n/X), then
Psi=sum mu(n)chi(n)[lambda H(n/X)+H(2n/X)]. Every principal algebraic
tail, coefficient zero and divisor remains.

A lower bound for the COMPLETE companion energy within
Ceps X^(2gamma+eps) of(1+lambda^2)(||E_m||_2^2+||D E_m||_2^2) is exactly
the desired upper bound for||Phi||_2^2. With alpha=||E_m||_2,
beta=lambda||D E_m||_2 and rho the normalized real inner product, its
deficit is(alpha-beta)^2+2alpha beta(1-rho); zero-norm cases use(221.1).
Both amplitude mismatch and full signed correlation must be estimated.
Positivity provides no upper saving for this deficit.

The complete future inverse is

    E_m(X)=-sum_(j>=1)lambda^-j Phi(2^j X),
    remainder O(X 2^(-Jr)).                              (221.2)

G216's actual O(X) bound pays the remainder and excludes the homogeneous
X^(r+1) solution. For shell Lp(dx/x), p=1,2 and exponent beta<r+1, the
recovery cost is1/(2^(r+1-beta)-1). Finite shifts give the converse, so
the complete two-channel bank preserves the Phi exponent class. Using
uncentered F instead introduces a principal squared scale X^(2r+2)
and requires correspondingly sharper relative deficit precision.

A stronger obstruction than constant-embedding isometry holds on the
ACTUAL full or retained-middle Jordan source. Let w_n=|mu(n)chi(n)K(n/X)|,
xi_n=mu(n)chi(n)K(n/X)/w_n when nonzero. Encode it as w_n v_n with
v_n=xi_n+t_n j and N(v_n)<=C^2, C fixed. The first channel is exactly
the original scalar source. Its pointwise absolute Gram price is

    B_+=sum_(d,e)w_d w_e |Re(v_d conjugate(v_e))|
          >=(sum_n w_n)^2/(4C^2).                       (221.3)

Proof: S=sum_n w_n v_n v_n^T is a positive real4x4 matrix, trace S>=W,
trace(S^2)>=(trace S)^2/4, and each |v_d dot v_e|<=C^2. Finite truncation
and monotone convergence cover the whole source. G216 gives
W=kappa_q X integral|K|+O(sqrt X), with positive leading constant.
The paid low/far absolute mass is O(X^gamma)+O(X^-1), so the SAME linear
mass remains in the exact middle. Therefore B_+ costs X^2 for both.
For q1/r2/m0 its lower constant is1/(64C^2 zeta(2)^2), while the
diagonal is at most C^2[X/(60zeta(2))+O(sqrt X)]. This also forces a
quadratic absolute off-diagonal price, not a signed-energy lower bound.

More generally, real dimension d, readout norm L and lift norm<=C give
L^2 B_+>=W^2/[d(CL)^2]. A bound of exponent2gamma would need
d(CL)^2 at least X^(2-2gamma-eps), up to constants. Reciprocal rescaling
does not change CL. This excludes only that POINTWISE absolute-Gram
certificate. Collective signed companion estimates, absolute values
after integration, or a fully paid changing dimension/readout remain open.
The full automorphic spinor function space is not four-dimensional.

The arithmetic/analytic escape conditions also stay explicit. Prime
images of a coprime-multiplicative quaternion lift commute and occupy
one complex slice, unless all are real; the commutator is twice the
cross product of imaginary parts. Ordered prime words need a new scalar
return. Even commuting quaternion coefficients need not commute with
n^-s in the chosen complex plane: (j2^-s)(j3^-s)=-2^-conjugate(s)3^-s,
generically different from-6^-s. A lawful holomorphic matrix series
uses CENTRAL complex n^-s and reflected coefficient functions, with
determinant Z(s)Z#(s)+W(s)W#(s), not a positive norm at generic height.
These distinctions do not obstruct pointwise real-scale energy identities.

The existing sixth-order SU(2) compact factor is exactly the user's
M(t conjugate(d)-t conjugate(c)j), with norm1. Its Iwasawa extraction is
not automatically an arithmetic group homomorphism. S44's earlier
phase-embedding seed remains an untested precursor, not a disproved idea.
The [[research revision] intake](../[research revision]/quaternion-norm-intake.md) records that prior
overlap and the elementary conventions. The new full calculation here
does not transfer a Jordan bound to a Gaussian/Hecke norm without a proof.
title: G221. The user's quaternion identity on the actual Jordan source

## G222. Exact prime-deletion inversion and the full signed readout

Fix an ordinary Dirichlet character chi modulo q and real X>=1. Let D_X
be the squarefree q-units n<=X, including1. It is a divisor downset.
For each unramified prime choose0<rho_p<=1, lambda_p=1-rho_p,
R_p=(2-rho_p)/rho_p. With row d and column n in D_X, define

    B(d,n)=1_(d|n) prod_(p|d)rho_p prod_(p|n/d)lambda_p,
    C(d,n)=1_(d|n) prod_(p|n)rho_p^-1 prod_(p|n/d)(-lambda_p).
                                                               (222.1)

Empty products and0^0 are1. Every intermediate divisor e between d,n
remains in D_X. Expanding BC or CB factors over primes of n/d, giving
the cancellation(lambda_p-lambda_p) at each missing prime and diagonal1.
Consequently both products equal the identity. Absolute column sums give

    ||B||_(1->1)=1,
    V(X):=||C||_(1->1)=max_(n in D_X) prod_(p|n)R_p.          (222.2)

For uniform fixed rho, V=R^K_X, K_X=max_D omega(n). The factorial bound
n>=(omega(n)+1)! implies K_X<=(1+o(1))log X/loglog X, so V=X^o(1).
The size downset is essential: a full prime cube would give the wrong
exponential price. Uniform moving rho_X=(log X)^-b instead costs
X^(b+o(1)); the matching lower factor count follows from primorials and
the ordinary [prime number theorem](https://dlmf.nist.gov/27.12).

For a FIXED prime-dependent sequence, the exact criterion is

    V(X)=X^o(1) iff log R_p/log p ->0.                       (222.3)

Necessity uses the column n=p at X=p. For sufficiency, given epsilon>0
choose P with R_p<=p^epsilon for p>P. Then the product is at most
[prod_(p<=P,p not|q)R_p]n^epsilon. The constant is independent of X.
Thus rho_p=min(1,(log p)^-b), b>0, may tend to0 while inversion remains
subpower. This is different from assigning the SAME rho_X to all primes.
For arbitrary X-dependent choices, the maximum in(222.2), not(222.3),
is the bill. No prime theorem is needed for the fixed-sequence criterion.

Apply B to nu(n)=chi(n) on D_X. The actual output and observer are

    b_X(d)=chi(d)prod_(p|d)rho_p
      *sum_(m<=X/d,(m,dq)=1)mu(m)^2 chi(m)prod_(p|m)lambda_p,
    h(d)=prod_(p|d)(-R_p),
    M_chi(X)=sum_(d in D_X)h(d)b_X(d).                       (222.4)

The cofactor phase chi(m), every natural zero, unit and cutoff remain.
Indeed summing over d|n gives prod_(p|n)(lambda_p-rho_p R_p)=mu(n).
The readout is bilinear, without a conjugation. For ANY full approximant
btilde_X, with e_X=b_X-btilde_X, one has

    |M_chi(X)|<=|sum_d h(d)btilde_X(d)|+V(X)||e_X||_1.       (222.5)

Under(222.3), complete every-epsilon bounds at exponent gamma for BOTH
right-hand quantities before the subpower loss give the same exponent
for M. Under a moving inverse cost X^b, the residual must pay b.
A selected label or omitted error does not have this return. No such
arithmetic approximation has been constructed here.

For one common gamma in(0,1) and every fixed ordinary character, this
Mertens estimate continues s int_1^infinity M_chi(x)x^(-s-1)dx=1/L(s,chi)
normally to Re s>gamma after an epsilon buffer. The continued identity
LF=1 excludes all regular zeros at every finite height. The principal
pole at1 becomes a reciprocal zero; imprimitive zeros and modulus
conventions remain those of [DLMF25.15](https://dlmf.nist.gov/25.15).
Constants and onsets may depend on the fixed character. No growing-q
uniformity or native Eisenstein-source transfer follows.

The inverse is affordable, but positive readout certificates fail in an
exact broader sense. For principal chi, b_X(d)>0, even when some rho_p=1,
because n=d contributes. For ANY moving retentions and positive diagonal
weights w_d,

    P_abs=sum_d |h(d)|b_X(d)
       =sum_(n in D_X)prod_(p|n)(3-2rho_p),
    #D_X<=P_abs<=3^K_X #D_X=X^(1+o(1)),
    ||w h||_2 ||b_X/w||_2>=P_abs.                          (222.6)

The minimum is attained by w_d^2=b_X(d)/|h(d)|. The same lower bound
holds for any conjugate Holder pair. The fixed-q squarefree count
#D_X=kappa_q X+O_q(sqrt X), kappa_q=(phi(q)/q)prod_(p not|q)(1-p^-2)>0,
follows by expanding mu^2 and counting q-units; it needs no PNT.
Thus arbitrary adaptive diagonal weights cannot make this principal
separable certificate power-small. This does not bound the signed readout
from below or exclude nonlocal signed norms or growing signed centering.

Uniform rho also gives the exact cutoff polynomial

    P_X(z)=sum_d b_X(d)z^omega(d)=Z_X(lambda+rho z),
    Z_X(z)=sum_(n in D_X)chi(n)z^omega(n), P_X(-R)=M_chi(X).
                                                               (222.7)

Its circle evaluation costs at most sqrt(sum_(j<=K_X)R^(2j)), subpower
for fixed rho. For principal chi all coefficients are nonnegative and
the prime layer has beta_0+beta_1>=pi_q(X), hence ||P_X||_circle>=pi_q(X)/sqrt2.
Deleting every original degree<=r, for fixed r, does not fix that norm:
products of r+1 distinct primes in((X/2)^(1/(r+1)),X^(1/(r+1))] supply
at least const X/log(X)^(r+1) mass in r+2 nonnegative coefficients.
Their l2 norm is at least mass/sqrt(r+2), uniformly in moving retention.
Other original layers only increase coefficients. This is a norm
obstruction, not an alternating-sum lower bound; signed quotient and
growing-layer methods survive. With varying rho_p there is generally no
single scalar z representing h: retain the labeled/multivariate readout.
title: G222. Exact prime-deletion inversion and the full signed readout

## G223. Critical small-prime payment with its exact margin debit

Use the complete ordinary-character source of
[G173](../[research revision]/wild62-integration.md): fixed tau>0,1/2<gamma<1,

    a(n)=mu(n)chi(n), g(v)=(2*pi*tau)^-1/2 exp(-v^2/(2tau)),
    U(y)=sum_(n>=1)a(n)g(log n-y), z(y)=e^(-gamma y)U(y),
    I_R=int_0^R y|z|^2, E_R=int_0^R |z|^2.

The coefficient identity a(n)log n=-sum_(d|n)chi(d)Lambda(d)a(n/d)
retains ALL prime powers, including cancellation at squareful n. It gives

    tau z'+(y+tau gamma)z+K1 z+K2 z=0,
    K1 z(y)=sum_p chi(p)log p p^-gamma z(y-log p),
    (tau/2)(|z(R)|^2-|z(0)|^2)+I_R+tau gamma E_R=Q1+Q2,
    Qj=-Re int_0^R conjugate(z)Kj z.                         (223.1)

G173 pays |Q2|<=eta I_R+B_eta for every eta>0 by its summable j>=2
coefficient norm, the complete Gaussian past and a fixed initial interval.
No unknown future bound is used. The same-output prime diagonal is
nonnegative and O(1): its coefficient is1 precisely at squarefree
q-units n=pm, the prime log-weights sum to at most log n, and

    int_R e^(-2gamma y)g(log n-y)^2dy
      =e^(tau gamma^2)n^(-2gamma)/(2sqrt(pi*tau)).

Here is a larger paid small-prime region. Fix a0>0 and set

    b=1/(1-gamma), Y(y)=a0(1+y)^b,
    kappa=a0^(1-gamma)/(1-gamma).

Assign equality to p<=Y(y). PNT and partial summation give
S_gamma(t)=sum_(p<=t)log p p^-gamma~t^(1-gamma)/(1-gamma).
The row sum is(kappa+o(1))y. Apply2|z(y)z(y-log p)|<=|z(y)|^2+|z(y-log p)|^2.
For the column put v=y-log p; the mask gives log p=O(log y), so for
any epsilon>0 and all large y, y<=v/(1-epsilon). Its column sum is at
most S_gamma(a0(1+v/(1-epsilon))^b)<=(kappa/(1-epsilon)+o(1))v.
Both half factors are present. The bounded initial region has finitely
many primes and a fixed bounded source interval. Therefore

    |Q_small(R)|<=(kappa+eta)I_R+B_eta, every R>=0.          (223.2)

The elementary theta(t)<=4(log2)t instead gives4(log2)kappa. This
critical mask is larger than G173's logarithmically reduced mask, but
its nonzero debit must be retained; it does not inherit the old zero
relative price or an unproved hard estimate for another mask.

Let H_a0,R be the ENTIRE p>Y(y), n!=pm expansion with literal summand

    -Re[conjugate(a(n))chi(p)a(m)] log p e^(-2gamma y)
                 *g(log n-y)g(log(pm)-y),                  (223.3)

integrated over0<=y<=R, all m,n>=1. Gaussian majorants justify the
compact-interval sums; diagonal and every complementary source remain.
If THIS jointly chosen mask has constants delta>kappa,B_chi,R0_chi with

    H_a0,R<=(1-delta)I_R+B_chi, every R>=R0_chi,             (223.4)

then pay eta=(delta-kappa)/4 in(223.2) and the higher powers to obtain

    (tau/2)|z(R)|^2+((delta-kappa)/2)I_R+tau gamma E_R<=B'.  (223.5)

Thus U(y)=O_chi(e^(gamma y)). Its complete bilateral transform equals
e^(tau s^2/2)/L(s,chi) initially on Re s>1 and continues normally to
Re s>gamma; the numerator never vanishes. This excludes every zero
at every finite height there, preserves the principal pole and all
natural zeros, and assumes no height-uniform numerator lower bound.
Gamma is common across the family; a0,delta and constants may depend
on a fixed character. This is a one-way ordinary-source return.

Choosing a0=[delta(1-gamma)/2]^(1/(1-gamma)) spends kappa=delta/2;
it does NOT manufacture the margin for the resulting mask. The targets
c=.12,.12515,1/6,1/4 require gamma=.88,.87485,5/6,3/4 and critical powers
25/3,20000/2503,6,4. The .12515 target exceeds conditional c11 by.0000040364.
None of the corresponding complete inequalities(223.4) is proved.

The generic leading coefficient is sharp even for a one-sided form.
For principal chi take arbitrary test input
f_T(y)=exp(i*pi*y/log Y_T)1_[T,T+sqrt T], Y_T=a0(1+T)^b.
Delays lose only O(log T/sqrt T) relative overlap, Y(y)/Y_T->1 uniformly,
and prime-weight mass below Y_T^(1-epsilon) is negligible. On the rest
the real phase tends to-1 as T then epsilon tend to their limits. Hence
-Re<f_T,K_small f_T>/int y|f_T|^2->kappa. A supercritical fixed power b'
instead gives asymptotic kappa T^(b'(1-gamma)-1), which diverges.
These are arbitrary inputs, not the actual z, and do not lower-bound its
signed form. Even granting |U(y)|<=C e^(beta y), gamma<beta<1, the
coarse absolute full-prime price has exponent1+beta-2gamma against
2beta-2gamma for I_R: the missing saving remains1-beta.
title: G223. Critical small-prime payment with its exact margin debit

## G224. Exact chirp and paired-character audits, with reconstruction paid

The two independent unselected audits preserve useful alternatives and
their exact limits. For z=a-i kappa, a>0, the analytic square root gives

    sqrt(z/(2*pi)) exp(t^2/(2z))
       *int_R exp(-z u^2/2+i t u)du=1,
    P_z(t)=(|z|/a)^1/2 exp(a t^2/(2|z|^2)).                 (224.1)

The first identity follows by the Gaussian Fourier integral and normal
continuation on Re z>0. The second is its exact completely absolute
price. On |t|<=T set E=a T^2/(2|z|^2)>0,
C=|kappa|T^2/(2|z|^2). Then P_z(T)=(1+(C/E)^2)^1/4 e^E
>=sqrt(C)e^E/sqrt(E)>=sqrt(2e C). A power-sized exterior chirp C=X^delta
therefore costs at least X^(delta/2) under absolute payment. Finite
insertion is legitimate; infinite insertion must pay its exterior
exponential against the original full tail. Signed/L2 use remains open.

For odd prime Q, A nonzero mod Q, c=(4A)^-1 and
G_A=sum_v e_Q(A v^2), completing the square gives
sum_v e_Q(A v^2+t v)=G_A e_Q(-c t^2), |G_A|^2=Q.
For actual residue sums B_r and F_v=sum_r B_r e_Q(c r^2+v r),

    S=sum_r B_r=G_A^-1 sum_v e_Q(A v^2)F_v,
    sum_v |F_v|^2=Q sum_r |B_r|^2,
    |S|^2=Q^-1 sum_(v,w)e_Q(A(v^2-w^2))F_v conjugate(F_w).
                                                               (224.2)

All crosses and natural zeros remain. The Cauchy bound |S|^2<=sum_v|F_v|^2
is generically sharp: B_r=1 gives equality Q^2. That is an ambient
coherent example, not a claim about the actual arithmetic residue array.
The four-point curvature of one bilinear t=mn channel has phase
c(m^2-m'^2)(n^2-n'^2)+v(m-m')(n-n'); complete channel recombination
restores multiplier1. A selected curved channel is not a full estimate.

The other audit distinguishes conjugate heights and observation loss.
F_barchi(s)=conjugate(F_chi(conjugate(s))) for F=1/L. A pole at rho maps
to conjugate(rho), not necessarily rho. For a Laurent vector with leading
coefficient v and continuous observation A(s), the leading squared signal
is v* A(rho)* A(rho) v. Positive semidefiniteness alone can annihilate v;
one needs coverage of actual residue directions, or a uniform lower
singular-value bound. A complete bank must keep every associated source.

At real x, the actual pair satisfies
||(M_chi(x),M_barchi(x))||^2=2|M_chi(x)|^2. This also holds with common
REAL weights; complex weights and heights must be conjugated as well.
A full every-epsilon shell-L1 pair estimate has the ordinary all-height
Abel return in G222, but is exactly the scalar estimate up to sqrt2.
The difference observation for a real character is identically zero.
Degenerating coordinate changes must pay their inverse. These adapters
preserve existing detector/curvature ancestry and supply no exponent gain.

The author's other selected tests retain the complete asymmetric
hyperbola identity u_U*u_V*chi=a-m_U-m_V+m_U*m_V*chi. Its principal
absolute long-long tuple price is at least const X when U,V<=sqrt X/2,
by pairs of squarefree q-units in(sqrt X/2,sqrt X]. This is not a signed
corner lower bound. Exterior-boundary and least-prime matching tests
duplicate G164-G165: the outgoing boundary remains, critical coordinates
need not be harmonic, and the matched character bulk a(n)(1-chi(p))
cannot be discarded outside the principal case. Their failures and all
22 untested cards are retained without broad rejection of the mechanisms.
title: G224. Exact chirp and paired-character audits, with reconstruction paid

## G225. Actual positive cofactor-hole prices, including after integration

Use the full G218 Gaussian over integers or Eisenstein integral ideals,
q_a=a or Na, with fixed eta,tau,S. Put c_a=mu_R(a)eta(a)1_((a,S)=1).
Let S+ add ALL natural-zero primes of the PRESENTED character, including
imprimitive modulus primes. On each entire shell[X,2X], choose arbitrary
nonnegative theta_Q with sum1 on radicals coprime to S, q_Q<=X^A,
fixed A>0. The choices may depend on X and the actual arithmetic source,
but are frozen in x. Define

    p(a)=sum_Q theta_Q 1_((a,Q)=1),
    K_X(a,b)=int_X^(2X)g(log(q_a/x))g(log(q_b/x))dx/x,
    A_theta=sum_(a,b)|Re(c_a conjugate(c_b))|K_X(a,b)p(rad(ab)),
    B_theta=sum_(a,b)|Re(c_a conjugate(c_b))|K_X(a,b)p(a)p(b).
                                                               (225.1)

The first is the average absolute-real Gram price of each hole field;
the second is that price for their averaged field. Both include diagonal
and both off-diagonal orientations. They are not the signed energies.

Uniformly over this entire family,

    X^2/log(2X)^2 << A_theta, B_theta << X^2.                (225.2)

Constants/onsets depend on R,S,eta,tau,A, not theta or Q. The lower bound
survives diagonal removal. This is a corollary of the G218 count and
G221 real-rank bound with a useful logarithmic refinement.

For Q*=rad(S+ Q), D(Q*)=prod_(p|Q*)(1+q_p^-1)^-1 satisfies

    D(Q*)^-1=sum_(d|Q*)q_d^-1
       <=sum_(q_d<=q_Q*)q_d^-1 << log(2q_Q*) << log(2X).

Partial summation of the elementary A_R(T)<<T proves this without PNT.
Subtract the uniform G218 squarefree counts at2X and X. The errors
are O(sqrt X log(2X)S_1/2(Q*)) over ideals and O(sqrt X d(Q*)) over
integers. The elementary small/large-prime split gives each factor sum
<<_delta q_Q*^delta; take delta=1/(4A). Thus errors are
O(X^(3/4)log(2X)), smaller than the main X/log(2X). No Q<=X
restriction is needed. Since g has a positive minimum on[-log2,log2],

    W_Q(x)=sum_a |c_a|1_((a,Q)=1)g(log(q_a/x))
       >>X/log(2X), every x in[X,2X],                     (225.3)

while the complete Gaussian majorant gives W_Q(x)<<x. No character
zero is replaced by a unit phase.

Regard xi_a=c_a/|c_a| as a unit vector in R^2 on its nonzero support.
With positive weights w_a, let M=sum_a w_a xi_a xi_a^T and W=sum_a w_a.
Then

    sum_(a,b)w_a w_b |xi_a dot xi_b|
      >=trace(M^2)>=W^2/2.                               (225.4)

The first step uses |t|>=t^2 on[-1,1]; the second uses two nonnegative
eigenvalues. All ACTUAL Mobius signs and character phases remain.
Apply it first to w_a=|c_a|1_((a,Q)=1)g, average theta and integrate.
Apply it separately to w_a=|c_a|p(a)g, whose mass is sum theta_Q W_Q.
These prove both lower bounds without comparing their kernels. For real
eta the constant1/2 can be1. Truncation, nonnegative convergence and the
Gaussian O(x) majorant justify every infinite sum and the O(X^2) upper bound.

The diagonals are sum_a |c_a|^2 K_X(a,a)p(a) and the same with p(a)^2.
Both are O(X), since0<=p<=1 and the squared Gaussian is a constant times
a narrower Gaussian. Subtracting them preserves(225.2) for large X.
The covariance kernels are not ordered entrywise: theta_1=theta_lm=1/2
gives joint/product1/2,1/4 at a=l,b=m, whereas theta_l=theta_m=1/2
gives0,1/4, for two distinct good primes and sufficiently large X.

For each pair the phase is independent of x and K_X is positive, so
int |Re(c_a conjugate(c_b))|g_a g_b dx/x
=|Re(c_a conjugate(c_b))K_X(a,b)| exactly. Hence taking pairwise real
absolute values AFTER integration gives the same scalar Gaussian price.
This identity does not discard cancellation in a collective signed sum,
extend to oscillatory joint-label kernels, or certify an arbitrary theta
as a zero detector. The latter needs its own complete fixed-source return.
G222's principal deletion-channel Holder floor and G127's different
curved-source obstruction retain their distinct priority and scope.
title: G225. Actual positive cofactor-hole prices, including after integration

## G226. A dimension-free obstruction after paying a common linear readout

This develops the user's quaternion proposal beyond the G221 bounded
rank-four argument. Root's [discovery and initial proof](linear-readout/root-draft.md)
tested growing dimension and delayed absolute values as possible escapes.
The [independent review](linear-readout/review.md) sharpened the initial
constant4/pi^2 to the sharp1/2 and clarified the complex-kernel and
variable-readout scopes. The earlier argument remains historical evidence.

Let H be ANY real Hilbert space, T:H->R^2 a bounded real-linear map with
norm L, and(v_a) a finite family. Define y_a=T v_a,
M=sum_a|y_a| and B=sum_(a,b)|<v_a,v_b>|, with all ordered pairs. Then

    L^2 B >= M^2/2.                                      (226.1)

No dimension or upper bound on individual vectors appears. To prove it,
let u_a=y_a/|y_a| when y_a!=0 and u_a=0 otherwise. Define A:R^2->H by
A e_j=sum_a u_(a,j)v_a. Its Hilbert-Schmidt norm satisfies

    ||A||_HS^2=sum_(a,b)<v_a,v_b><u_a,u_b><=B,
    TA=sum_a |y_a|u_a u_a^T,
    M^2/2<=trace((TA)^2)=||TA||_HS^2<=L^2||A||_HS^2.

The positive2x2 operator has trace M and squared eigenvalue sum at least
M^2/2. This proves(226.1). Equality occurs for
T=identity on R^2, v_1=e_1,v_2=e_2. If all images lie on one real line,
the constant improves to1. More generally a target R^r gives the sharp
constant1/r, depending on OUTPUT dimension rather than lift dimension.
This is not the false termwise inequality
|<Tv_a,Tv_b>|<=L^2|<v_a,v_b>|.

Separate maps per index do not meet this hypothesis: v_i=e_i in R^n,
T_i(v)=v_i gives B=n, M=n and separate norms1. The COMMON recovery
v->sum_i v_i has norm sqrt(n), restoring the missing bill.

For an infinite family, apply(226.1) to every finite subset and take
nonnegative limits. No convergence of an infinite vector sum is needed
for this extended inequality. Each vector and readout must still exist.
The result includes arbitrary dimension, additional quaternion components,
and X-dependent choices of the common map, once its norm is paid.

Pointwise, if T_x v_a(x)=c_a K(q_a/x), then

    L_x^2 sum_(a,b)|<v_a(x),v_b(x)>|
       >=(1/2)[sum_a|c_a K(q_a/x)|]^2.                    (226.2)

For the G221 quaternion lift w_a(xi_a+t_a j), first-complex-coordinate
projection has L_x=1. Thus the actual full/middle source has quadratic
pointwise absolute price even WITHOUT a bound on t_a. The old necessary
dimension/readout tradeoff remains valid but is weaker: growing the
dimension does not reduce the price after a common linear recovery is paid.

There is a corresponding after-integration theorem. Put I=[X,2X],
measure dx/x and length ell=log2. Let v_a belong to its direct-integral
real Hilbert space, and let T_x be measurable common recovery maps with
essential supremum norm L_X<infinity on the shell. Assume

    T_x v_a(x)=c_a K(q_a/x),
    J(t)=int_1^2 K(t/u)du/u.

The common map Tcal(v)=int_I T_x v(x)dx/x has norm at most L_X sqrt(ell)
and sends v_a to c_a J(q_a/X). Apply(226.1) in the direct integral:

    L_X^2 ell sum_(a,b)|int_I <v_a(x),v_b(x)>dx/x|
       >=(1/2)[sum_a |c_a J(q_a/X)|]^2.                  (226.3)

All absolute values on the left are AFTER pair integration. A fixed
common ambient H is sufficient; measurable Hilbert bundles also work
when the stated direct integral and maps are well defined. It suffices
to apply the argument to finite central subsets; infinite absolute prices
then dominate those finite ones. Arbitrary x-dependent lifts are allowed.

The variable bound int_I ||T_x||^2 dx/x also bounds Tcal's squared norm,
but it does NOT automatically pay full shell-L2 reconstruction. For the
actual source-energy certificate the uniform L_X above is sufficient:
||sum_a T_x v_a||_(L2)^2<=L_X^2||sum_a v_a||_(L2(H))^2<=L_X^2 B_after
when the sums/convergence required for that upper estimate are justified.
If no such finite reconstruction bill is available, do not claim a
source upper bound from the averaged-functional inequality alone.

The right side has quadratic order for the exact Jordan source, including
its retained middle. Its fixed kernel is generally COMPLEX for nonreal
chi, and G215 gives K(t)=e^-t+O(e^-2t), so K is continuous, nonzero and
tends to0 at infinity. More generally these three properties imply J is
not identically zero: in logarithmic coordinates J'=K(t)-K(t/2); J=0
would force K(t)=K(2t), hence K=0 by repeated scaling to infinity.
Choose a fixed interval[a,b] in(0,infinity) on which |J|>=k>0. The
fixed-q squarefree count gives

    sum_(d>=1)|mu(d)chi(d)J(d/X)| >>_(q,K) X.              (226.4)

For G215's middle, d in[aX,bX] lies in x^alpha<d<=2x log x for EVERY
x in[X,2X] once X is large, because alpha<1. Thus these central vectors
have exactly the same integrated image c_d J(d/X); they alone prove the
same lower bound in(226.3). No omitted tail, principal main term or
varying-cutoff identity has been discarded. The actual compensated K,
not the uncentered Jordan source, is used.

For the G218 Gaussian, positivity directly gives |J(t)| bounded below
on[1,2]. Fixed holes give mass >>X; polynomial-sized holes, or their
positive normalized field averages, give >>X/log(2X) by G225, with all
presented character zeros retained. Applying(226.3) separately to each
hole also permits a positive average of its complete lifted price.
No arbitrary oscillatory joint-label kernel is identified with that
positive-mask construction.

These are TOTAL-price lower bounds. To conclude the same for the absolute
off-diagonal, also pay the diagonal. In G221's bounded lifts with fixed
C, sum_a int_I ||v_a||^2=O(C^2 X), so the quadratic lower bound survives
its removal. Without such a bound an unbounded lift may move the bill
onto its diagonal; no off-diagonal assertion is then made.

The complete returned shell-L2 target gamma=1-c requires energy exponent
2-2c. The paid source-index absolute-Gram price above has exponent at
least2, leaving deficit2c: .24 at c=.12, .2502919272 at conditional c11,
.25030 at c=.12515,1/3 at c=1/6 and1/2 at c=1/4. G215/G218 supply their
own L2-to-L1 and all-height returns; the price theorem proves none of
the necessary signed estimates and imports no cross-family transfer.

The scope matters: one vector per actual source coefficient, a common
linear recovery, the COMPLETE pairwise absolute Gram, and a paid norm.
Cancellation inside blocks before the absolute value, full signed
companion comparisons, nonlinear reconstruction, or genuinely different
X-dependent profiles with a proved return remain open. The theorem is
not a lower bound on the actual signed source energy. It strengthens
G221's finite-dimensional price and closes its generic after-integration
escape for these fixed Gaussian/Jordan profiles and common recoveries;
it does not reject quaternion or matrix approaches as a whole.

## G227. An actual twisted inverse and its cofactor-resolved observation

Fix an ordinary Dirichlet character chi modulo a fixed positive integer q.
Let S_N={a<=N: a squarefree, (a,q)=1}, ordered increasingly, with N>=1 an
integer. Write E_ad=1_(d|a) and M=diag(mu(a)). Every divisor interval of S_N
is complete, so finite Mobius inversion gives E^-1=M E M. With

    A_chi=E diag(mu(d) conjugate(chi(d))) E^T,
    (A_chi)_ab=prod_(p|(a,b))(1-conjugate(chi(p))),

the diagonal is invertible because |chi(d)|=1 on the actual labels. Therefore

    (A_chi^-1)_ab=mu(a)mu(b)
                   sum_(d in S_N,[a,b]|d)mu(d)chi(d).       (227.1)

The pairing and transpose are bilinear. A_chi is generally complex symmetric,
not Hermitian. Its (1,1) inverse entry is exactly M_chi(N)=sum_(n<=N)mu(n)chi(n).
Simply phase-gauging the real coprimality matrix would leave that observed
inverse entry untwisted, so it does not establish (227.1).

Put g=(a,b), l=[a,b]. Writing d=lm in (227.1), squarefreeness forces (m,l)=1,
and mu(a)mu(b)mu(l)=mu(g). Hence

    (A_chi^-1)_ab=mu(g)chi(l) M_(chi,lq)(N/l),
    M_(chi,h)(y)=sum_(m<=y,(m,h)=1)mu(m)chi(m).             (227.2)

This is zero for l>N. In particular the first inverse row and complete
residual identity, for ANY proposed column z and r=e1-A_chi z, are

    R_N(a)=chi(a) M_(chi,aq)(N/a),  |R_N(a)|<=floor(N/a),
    M_chi(N)=z1+sum_(a in S_N) R_N(a)r(a),
    B_N(z):=sum_a |R_N(a)r(a)|
       <=W_N(z):=N sum_a |r(a)|/a.                         (227.3)

All coordinates remain. If r is supported on a>N/H, H>=1, this costs at most
H||r||1. A global inverse operator norm is therefore an unnecessarily large
default price for a residual known to live on large labels. The exact signed
sum in (227.3) remains available; its absolute bound is only a sufficient bill.

For fixed 0<gamma<1, a complete every-epsilon bound for |z1|+B_N(z), or the
stronger explicit |z1|+W_N(z), by N^(gamma+epsilon) gives the same Mertens
bound. The alternative every-epsilon integral_1^X |M_chi(t)|^2 dt/t bound
by X^(2gamma+epsilon) also suffices. On each dyadic shell Cauchy bounds
the Abel integral and all its fixed derivatives, with a positive exponent
buffer on any compact subset of Re(s)>gamma. The normally convergent function

    s integral_1^infinity M_chi(t)t^(-s-1)dt

equals 1/L(s,chi) on Re(s)>1. Continuing the identity with L excludes regular
zeros in Re(s)>gamma at every finite height. At the principal pole s=1 the
reciprocal has a zero. Natural character zeros stay in the coefficients.
Constants may depend on the fixed character and epsilon; no growing-conductor
or Hecke assertion follows. This is a complete return from an OPEN estimate.

Two concrete inverse cautions survive. In the principal N=2 case the signed
coprimality matrix [[1,-1],[-1,0]] is invertible but its nuisance block [0]
is singular and its inverse (1,1) entry is0. A Schur formula requiring that
block inverse fails. On m distinct prime labels the matrix is J-I, full rank
for m>=2, while rank-one J has operator residual1 and scalar residual at most
||u||2||v||2. Exact rank alone therefore does not rule out a paid approximation.
title: G227. An actual twisted inverse and its cofactor-resolved observation

## G228. The sharp depth of a low-omega-completed inverse column

Fix 0<beta<1. For 1<=T<=beta N and an integer k>=0 define

    F_(T,k)(d)=1_(d<=T OR omega(d)<=k),
    z=E^-T (chi(d) F_(T,k)(d))_d.

The first row of E^-T is mu(d), and multiplying by A_chi cancels chi against
its conjugate. Using sum_(d|a)mu(d)=1_(a=1) gives the exact identities

    z1=sum_(d in S_N)mu(d)chi(d) F_(T,k)(d),
    r(a)=sum_(d|a,d>T,omega(d)>k)mu(d).                     (228.1)

If omega(a)=k+1 and a>T, all proper divisors are included, so r(a)=mu(a).
For a>N/2 its cofactor observation is exactly R_N(a)=chi(a).
Let b_k be the product of the first k primes not dividing q, b_0=1, and put
alpha=max(beta,1/2). Every prime p in (alpha N/b_k,N/b_k] not dividing b_k q
gives a distinct actual coordinate a=b_k p with |R_N(a)r(a)|=1. Thus

    B_N(z)<=W_N(z),
    B_N(z)>=#{alpha N/b_k<p<=N/b_k : p prime, p not|b_k q}. (228.2)

The second line is an exact finite inequality, possibly zero for small N.
For fixed k, the ordinary prime number theorem gives the lower asymptotic
(1-alpha)N/(b_k log N). Correcting primes, semiprimes or any other fixed number
of omega layers has not made this absolute residual small at any exponent<1.

There is also a matching upper bound for growing depth. Set h=k+1,
H_N=sum_(m<=N)1/m and A_N=sum_(p<=N)1/p, including conductor primes if desired.
Taking the absolute value in (228.1) and exchanging the finite divisor sums,

    W_N(z)<=N H_N sum_(d<=N,d squarefree,omega(d)>=h)1/d
           <=N H_N sum_(j>=h) A_N^j/j!
           <=N H_N exp(A_N) A_N^h/h!.                     (228.3)

An unordered j-prime set occurs j! times in A_N^j. Admitting repeated primes
and products above N only enlarges the positive sum. The last inequality
uses (h+r)!>=h!r!. This pays EVERY residual coordinate and is uniform in T.

Ordinary PNT and partial summation give p_j~j log j and A_N=O(loglog N).
The [NIST reference](https://dlmf.nist.gov/27.12) records the prime asymptotics;
the consequences here are derived from them. Removing fixed q's finitely
many primes changes indices by a bounded amount, so log b_k~k log k as k grows.
If k~kappa log N/loglog N for fixed 0<kappa<1, then
b_k=N^(kappa+o(1)), while its largest prime is O(log N). The prime interval
in (228.2) lies above all these factors eventually; its endpoint is
N^(1-kappa+o(1)). PNT on a fixed-ratio interval, together with (228.3) and
log(h!)=h log h-h+O(log h), proves

    B_N(z)=N^(1-kappa+o(1)),  W_N(z)=N^(1-kappa+o(1)).      (228.4)

These are logarithmic exponents, uniform for 1<=T<=beta N, not fixed-k
logarithmic asymptotic formulas. If k=o(log N/loglog N), both exponents are1.

More generally fix ONE sequence k_N>=0 and ONE cutoff sequence
1<=T_N<=beta N for all sufficiently large N, independently of epsilon. For 0<gamma<1,

    B_N(z_N)<<_epsilon N^(gamma+epsilon) for EVERY epsilon>0
    iff W_N(z_N)<<_epsilon N^(gamma+epsilon) for EVERY epsilon>0
    iff liminf_N k_N loglog N/log N >= 1-gamma.             (228.5)

For sufficiency, bound the nonnegative tail in (228.3) at any smaller depth
a log N/loglog N with 0<a<1-gamma and then let a approach1-gamma according
to epsilon. For necessity, if the liminf is smaller, choose such an a above
it. Along infinitely many N the primorial is at most N^(a+o(1)), so (228.2)
has exponent at least1-a, contradicting a sufficiently small fixed epsilon.
No short-interval or growing-modulus prime theorem is used.

Equality in (228.5) is sufficient for the residual bill alone. It does not
pay z1. In fact, with D_N the number of omitted coefficients,

    z1=M_chi(N)-sum_(d in S_N,d>T,omega(d)>=h)mu(d)chi(d),
    D_N<=sum_(n<=N)binom(omega(n),h)
        =sum_(d<=N,d squarefree,omega(d)=h)floor(N/d)
        <=N A_N^h/h!.                                    (228.6)

Once (228.5) holds, the every-epsilon exponent-gamma estimate on z1 is
equivalent to that on M_chi(N). The retained coordinate still carries the
arithmetic problem. At the c11 benchmark the residual's threshold is
liminf k_N loglog N/log N >= .1251459636; the full certificate is still open.

The lower bounds concern COMPLETE ABSOLUTE bills of this SPECIFIC column
family. They do not lower-bound the complete signed residual, Mertens sum,
any arbitrary approximant or a Gaussian energy. Higher residual layers need
not have a common sign: for k=1,T=11,a=30, r(30)=mu(15)+mu(30)=0.

The ancestry is the first-unpaid-layer argument in W43/[research revision] and [research revision]'s
fixed-layer circle obstruction. W43's Newton defect includes prime powers
and factorial multiplicities; at T=1,k=1 its order-two defect at pq is2,
where (228.1) is1. G78/G83-G85 already paid their own growing-order Gaussian
restoration, so that older obligation is not reopened. The new scoped result
is the cofactor certificate's exact depth threshold and its remaining z1
obligation, rather than a new generic lesson about truncation.
title: G228. The sharp depth of a low-omega-completed inverse column

## G229. A full Walsh source with its Gaussian and Euler returns paid

This section concerns the principal coprime Gaussian P_Y of G25-G30. Fix
tau>0, Y=floor(X^.495), B_X=2X exp(C sqrt(log X)), with fixed C>0. The Boolean
cube uses ALL primes5<=p<=B_X. For labels u,v put d(u)=prod_p p^u_p and

    K(u,v)=(-1)^(|u|+|v|)1_(u and v disjoint),
    W_x(u,v)=1_(d(u)>Y,d(v)>Y,d(u)d(v)<=B_X)
      *sum_(ell<=B_X/(d(u)d(v)))(-1)^(ell+1)
           g_tau(log(d(u)d(v)ell/x)).

Then Z_X(x)=sum K W_x is the literal output-truncated ordered source.
Shared-prime zeros, p=2,3 exclusions, both strict cuts and every ell sign
remain. With K_0 cube sites and an unnormalized Walsh transform in BOTH
variables, finite orthogonality proves

    Z_X(x)=2^(-2K_0) sum_(alpha,beta) Khat(alpha,beta) What_x(alpha,beta).
                                                               (229.1)

There is no complex conjugation in this bilinear identity. Locally,
H=[[1,1],[1,-1]], T=[[1,-1],[-1,0]], and H T H=[[-1,1],[1,3]]. All four
dual gate entries are nonzero. Sparsity of the complete transformed mask
would require its own theorem; the global prime cube is not one divisor cube.

The original d3 coefficient majorant bounds the discarded output field,
uniformly on x in[X,2X], by X^(1-C^2/(2tau)+o(1)). The counting Jacobian
is included in that exponent. Choose C with this exponent below the desired
gamma>1/2. G27 independently pays |P_Y-F6|<<X^(.495+delta), delta<gamma-.495.
G28 then uses fixed Euler convolutions and their inverses, with direct
factor (1-z)^2 at2,3 and (1-z)^2/(1-2z) at p>=5. Their weighted absolute
coefficient sums converge for every fixed sigma>1/2; the original exceptional
prime2 coefficients1,-3,2 remain. Apply this norm transfer to the FIXED F6
and G_tau fields, then apply each shell's own frozen Y comparison.

Thus a COMPLETE every-epsilon shell L2 bound for (229.1) at exponent gamma
would return the original fixed Gaussian G3 and its zeta zero exclusion.
The changing finite cube has no independently asserted Mellin transform.
Both copies, all dual modes, their cross terms and the complementary field
remain. An ordinary-character or Hecke extension is an additional theorem.
No arithmetic estimate for the whole right side has been proved.

## G230. Paid ambient realizations and two independent audits

If A=alpha P U Q with U unitary and P,Q contractions, alpha>=||A|| follows
by submultiplicativity. For C=A/alpha a contraction, the Halmos block
[[C,(I-CC*)^(1/2)],[(I-C*C)^(1/2),-C*]] is unitary; the defect intertwining
identity proves it directly. It realizes the optimum alpha=||A||. For
selfadjoint C its square is I, whereas C^2=I-(I-C^2); repeated use must
retain the returning defect or intermediate physical projections. A
source-specific approximation remains possible, with the full scalar
residual bounded by delta||u||2||v||2 when its operator error is delta.

The signed local gate T is a diagonal sign gauge of [[1,1],[1,0]], so their
singular values agree. The indefinite J=[[-2,-1],[-1,2]] satisfies T^TJT=-J,
yet v=(phi,-1), phi=(1+sqrt5)/2, is J-null and Tv=phi v. Conserved flux
does not bound that positive observation. For a selfadjoint K, the Cayley
unitary V=(K-iI)(K+iI)^-1 has (I-V)^-1=(I-iK)/2 and inverse norm
sqrt(1+||K||^2)/2. No selfadjoint claim is licensed for complex A_chi.

The protected S28 audit diagonalizes the disjointness gate orthogonally.
For K_0 sites its eigenvalues are (-1)^j phi^(K_0-2j), with binomial
multiplicity, and squared Frobenius norm3^K_0. Writing the FULL physical
boundary in that basis preserves its Frobenius norm; the generic contraction
bill is3^(K_0/2)||W||F. A product-only weight counts each ordered prime
allocation and produces mu(n)chi(n)2^omega(n), not the original Mertens
coefficient. A single n-divisor cube has omega(n)=O(log n/loglog n);
that does not bound the global prime set of every n<=X.

The uniform S09 audit uses the connected prime-adjoining graph on S_N.
For (Bf)_(n,pn)=f(pn)+chi(p)f(n), write f(n)=a(n)g(n), a(n)=mu(n)chi(n).
Then ker B=span(a). In ANY complete identity w=lambda e1+B^T t, pairing
with a forces lambda=sum_n w_n a(n). A rooted prime-deletion tree constructs
t from complete signed subtree sums. If r=w-lambda e1-B^Tt, then

    |sum_n w_n a(n)|<=|lambda|+||r||1,
    inf_(lambda,t)(|lambda|+||w-lambda e1-B^Tt||1)=|sum_n w_n a(n)|.
                                                               (230.1)

The upper equality chooses the exact signed target as lambda; the lower is
the triangle inequality. This leaves constructive arithmetic certificates
eligible, but feasibility alone hides the original target in a coordinate.

All these bills concern their named positive, absolute or generic ambient
arguments. They leave complete signed arithmetic cancellation open. The
review's S28/S09 audits froze before author outcomes, and all30 original
cards and dispositions remain in the retained source reports. Conditional
c11 and the separate PR15/F0/positive-slot/external-admission gaps are unchanged.
title: G230. Paid ambient realizations and two independent audits

Retain all shared primes, natural character zeros and ordered factors. Write f_x(n)=exp(-n/x^b-i(n/x)^k) and F_u(x)=sum_(n>=1)u(n)f_x(n).
Freeze theta=max(b/2,2-b), rho=(k-2gamma)/(k-2), L=X^gamma, M=X^rho, R=X^(1-gamma), U_r=X^(gamma/2)/r. Let b1(v)=(q1*chi)(v)=chi(v)(1-p 1_(p|v)). The entire residual is
T_(p,X)(x)=sum_(2<=r<=R)t_p(r) sum_(a>U_r,b'>U_r,v>=1; r^2 a b' v<=M) m(a)m(b')b1(v)f_x(r^2 a b' v).
The strict inverse cuts make r^2ab'>L automatic and imply v<X^(rho-gamma); no new coprimality condition is imposed.
For j=1 and for j=2 separately, every epsilon>0 and all sufficiently large dyadic X,
||sum_(L<n<=M)h_p(n)f_x(n)-T_(p,X)(x)||_(j,X) <<_(chi,p,b,k,gamma,epsilon) X^(gamma+epsilon).
Thus the respective complete masked-source and T_(p,X) every-epsilon growth hypotheses are equivalent for each norm separately. L1 control is not asserted to imply L2 control.
The whole large-root source satisfies ||F_((t_p 1_(r>R) on squares)*c_M)||_(j,X) << X log(2R)/R+X^theta log^2(2X). This pays the actual dilation mismatch, not an exact x/r^2 substitution. Its uniform coefficient-square envelope pays the removed prefix and full tail; the original L<n<=M mask is restored before the norm triangle. The complete frozen Type I bank has d<=L, |A_d|<=C_p tau_4(d), and mean-zero periodic b1. The complete periodic-cofactor result G191 pays that entire bank; its coefficient envelope and divisor epsilon pay every prefix/tail complement. At gamma=2/3 the p-dependent short-support edge is retained and paid. At gamma=theta logarithms are absorbed only through every-epsilon bounds.

raw_source_record.statement:
Fix distinct unramified primes p,ell. Let m(n)=mu(n)chi(n), s(r^2)=chi(r)^2 and s(n)=0 off squares, Q_p=delta_1-p chi(p)delta_p, B_p=delta_1-p chi(p)^2 delta_(p^2), and h_p=Q_p*(B_p*s*s-delta_1)*m. Then the exact complete aggregate
v=B_ell*Q_ell*h_p-B_p*Q_p*h_ell=Q_p*Q_ell*(B_p-B_ell)*m
has eight actual shifts: v(n)=sum_(d|n)a_d m(n/d). In the order d=p^2,p^3,p^2 ell,p^3 ell,ell^2,p ell^2,ell^3,p ell^3, a_d/chi(d)=-p,p^2,p ell,-p^2 ell,ell,-p ell,-ell^2,p ell^2. Shared primes and character zeros remain literal. The finite readout cost is (p+ell)(1+p)(1+ell); this is not power sparsity.
For Re(z)>1,
D_v(z)=[(1-chi(p)p^(1-z))(1-chi(ell)ell^(1-z))(chi(ell)^2 ell^(1-2z)-chi(p)^2 p^(1-2z))]/L(z,chi).
The numerator never vanishes in 1/2<Re(z)<1. Cumulative coefficient-square mass is O_(p,ell)(Y).
Fix rho=(k-2gamma)/(k-2)<b, L=X^gamma, M=X^rho, and K_(v,X)(x)=sum_(L<n<=M)v(n)exp(-n/x^b-i(n/x)^k). Every shifted realization keeps exp(-d n/x^b), phase (d n/x)^k and the local cuts L/d<n<=M/d; it is not an unpriced scale-x/d observation. The complete prefix and tail give ||F_v-K_(v,X)||_(1,X)+||F_v-K_(v,X)||_(2,X) << X^gamma. The respective full/core growth hypotheses are equivalent in each norm separately; L2 is stronger than the least L1 premise, and no L1-to-L2 implication is claimed.
The least unpaid source premise is ||K_(v,X)||_(1,X) <<_epsilon X^(gamma+epsilon), for every epsilon and all sufficiently large dyadic shells. With a fixed Taylor order K satisfying 1-K(b-1)<gamma, the complete Mellin descent returns ordinary fixed-character zero exclusion above gamma. Existing higher-Taylor descent receives its original credit; this is not a new continuation theorem. The classical line-1 endpoint and permitted principal pole are paid independently; alternatively all three pairs of a fixed covering triple need their own aggregate hypotheses. No earlier conditional boundary is used.
A separately stronger L2 device keeps all damping moments: choose fixed J>=1 with (J+1)rho-Jb<=gamma; let Delta=X^k, t0=(1+2^(-k))/(2X^k), Psi_J(z)=sum_(0<=j<J)z^j/(j!)^2 and W_X(n,n')=(1-|n'^k-n^k|/Delta)_+.
Q_X=2 Re sum_(L<n<n'<=M) v(n)conj(v(n')) exp(i t0(n'^k-n^k)) W_X(n,n') Psi_J(nn'/X^(2b)); D_X=sum_(L<n<=M)|v(n)|^2 Psi_J(n^2/X^(2b)); E_X=D_X+Q_X>=0.
The exact remaining hypothesis for this L2 device is the one-sided Q_X<=C_epsilon X^(2gamma+epsilon), not an absolute bound on each correlation. Negative Q_X helps. D_X=O(M) is paid because rho<b<=2gamma, and ||K_(v,X)||_(2,X)^2 <<_(k,J) E_X+X^(2gamma). Thus this hypothesis implies the complete L1 premise. All 64 mixed dilation pairs, their coefficients, local cuts, character zeros, ordering and triangular/Taylor weights remain.
The established source-reported bound, using the Green–Tao polynomial Mobius theorem with original-paper credit, is E_X <<_D M+X^2(log X)^(-D) for every fixed D>0. At gamma=0.8748 the required squared exponent is 1.7496, leaving a 0.2504 power gap. A fixed logarithmic saving does not close it. The interval-energy observation contains the macroscopic filtered-Mertens mean square; finite erasure and higher fixed degree do not bypass that requirement. A complementary maximal-prefix/two-source inverse criterion is an additional conditional route, not a supplied power estimate. No achieved c increase or theorem at gamma=1/2 is asserted.

Repeated mean-zero periodic primitives give the complete integer-row bound O_J(S^(1-J) exp(-cN/X^b)(1+Tphase)^J), without discarded endpoints. raw_source_record.statement:
For every bounded complex sequence |a(n)|<=1, fix R=4/3 and A_j=R^j,I_j={n>=1:A_j<=n<A_(j+1)}. Given a shell X>=e and fixed E>0, choose r=max(1,ceil((E+1)log X/log3)), N=floor(2(E+2)X log X), J=floor(log N/log R), before live x in[X,2X]. Retain the exact moments C_(j,m)=sum_(n in I_j,n<=N)a(n)((n-A_j)/A_j)^m and complete synthesis S_X(x)=sum_(j=0)^J exp(-A_j/x)sum_(m=0)^(r-1)(-A_j/x)^m C_(j,m)/m!. Then sup_[X,2X]|sum_(n>=1)a(n)exp(-n/x)-S_X(x)| <<_E X^(-E), with O_E(log^2 X) moments. Every within-cell order, last-cell cut, original sign/natural zero and cross-cell interaction remains. The degree-uniform finite error for any integer r>=1,N is <=(1/3)^r(Rx+2), obtained by the complete unimodal sum of t^r exp(-t), integral r! and at most two peak values. The omitted integer tail is <=(2X+1)exp(-N/(2X)).
For actual a(n)=mu(n)chi(n), fixed ordinary chi, a complete every-epsilon shell L1 bound ||S_X||_1 << X^(gamma+epsilon), with0<gamma<1 common to the asserted fixed-character family, transfers to the fixed Laplace source. Its full Mellin transform Gamma(s)/L(s,chi), paid left tail and nonvanishing Gamma then exclude all finite-height zeros of every multiplicity above gamma, with the principal pole and imprimitive factors retained. The signed synthesis bound is unproved; absolute separate moment payment only gives exponent1.
Coarse logarithmic cell balance is insufficient: assign +1 to the first floor(#I_j/2) integers, -1 to the last, and0 to any central leftover. Every cell sum vanishes, while the ordinary Dirichlet series has a simple pole at1 of residue log(49/48)/log(4/3). The one-cell Riemann error is O_K(R^(-j Re(s))) on compact subsets of Re(s)>0, giving a holomorphic remainder. This is a bounded integer countermodel, not a Mobius counterexample. For actual mu(n)chi(n), the absolute one-mode rounding bill is asymptotic in order to eta X uniformly for X^(-1/2+delta)<=eta<=eta0, with fixed q,delta>0 and sufficiently small fixed eta0. That absolute price does not lower-bound signed rounding error.
The mechanism refines earlier Gaussian compression and signed transport; the moment count is not an arithmetic algorithm or an improvement over the earlier Gaussian rank. No arithmetic power saving or c increase is established.

The unique compact adjacent-gap current is J_N(u)=M(exp u) for0<=u<log(N+1), zero outside. For every absolutely continuous complex f, int f dnu_N=-int J_N f'. For nonnegative integrable w, sup_(f(log(N+1))=0,|f'|<=w)|int f dnu_N|=int|J_N|w. Equality uses f'=-w conjugate(J_N)/|J_N| where J_N is nonzero; hence nonreal phases are retained. Splitting longer line edges into adjacent gaps proves no routing can reduce this metric cost. The endpoint ghost is retained exactly and is not an estimate of M(N).
For w=1 the norm is int_1^(N+1)|M(t)|dt/t. If for a common0<gamma<1 every fixed character and every epsilon satisfy int_X^(2X)|M(t)|dt/t <<_(chi,epsilon)X^(gamma+epsilon) on all sufficiently large dyadic shells, then H(s)=s int_1^infinity M(t)t^(-s)dt/t is holomorphic for Re(s)>gamma, including every fixed derivative, and agrees initially with1/L(s,chi). The complete Abel identity excludes all finite-height zeros of every multiplicity there, treating the principal pole by its reciprocal zero. It does not require first deducing a pointwise Mertens bound of exponent gamma. The elementary coefficient-continuity argument only yields the weaker pointwise exponent(1+gamma)/2.
The exact norm identity supplies no independent arithmetic upper bound. Endpoint cell balance alone leaves linear current cost for the bounded countermodel of G237. raw_source_record.statement:
For a finite matrix K retaining the entire original labeled source, put A=[[0,K],[K*,0]]. Represent each nonzero contribution by a directed edge e, with computational reverse bar(e) of weight conjugate(w_e); parallel labels remain distinct. Define(Sf)_e=f_head(e),(Tg)_v=sum_(tail(e)=v)w_e g_e,(Rg)_e=w_bar(e)g_bar(e). Then A=TS and B=ST-R is the exact weighted nonbacktracking lift. Where all displayed inverses exist, F(z)=I-zT(I+zR)^(-1)S satisfies F(z)^(-1)=I+zT(I-zB)^(-1)S. Each reverse pair has R^2=|w_e|^2I, so the eliminated operator has diagonal1+sum_tail z^2|w_e|^2/(1-z^2|w_e|^2) and off-diagonal contributions-z w_e/(1-z^2|w_e|^2). Both backtrack diagonals and changed off-diagonal weights remain.
The original projected source y*Kx is the coefficient of z in y0*F(z)^(-1)x0, with x0=(0,x),y0=(y,0). A Cauchy return must pay its actual contour, projected resolvent, lift norms and exceptional parameters. The generic lift bounds are ||T||^2=max_v sum_tail|w_e|^2 and ||S||^2=max_v #{head(e)=v}, counting parallel labels. For a d-leaf unit-weight star, B^2=0 but ||B||=d-1 and ||A||=sqrt d. Thus spectral radius alone cannot bound the original source norm. This is a generic graph counterexample, not an arithmetic native-H lower bound or obstruction on its actual source range.
In the original native-H application retain the full coefficients, original additive character, both complete mark projectors, natural zeros, parallel labels, signed d and g,g' sums, true-core weights and source complement. The fixed-u,v raw K+N deficit at N=K Z^.003 differs from the full all-g K+NG deficit with G=Z^.001; neither the .003 nor .004 saving is proved by this identity. The outer squared scalar N^(-1)G^(-2) and original signed near-band restoration remain. An actual projected resolvent estimate with complete source return is still required; no ordinary-character identification, arithmetic power saving or c gain follows.

raw_source_record.statement:
Set a(m)=mu(m)chi(m), D_m={d|Q:md<=N}, d_m=|D_m| and C_m=sum_(d in D_m)mu(d)chi(d). Then M_chi(N)=sum_(n<=N)mu(n)chi(n)=sum_m a(m)C_m. Every original zero and shortened cutoff is retained. B_P(N)=sum_m|C_m|>=pi(N)-pi(N/2)-|P|-omega(q). For all sufficiently large N the dyadic-prime term is >=(log2/12)N/log N; hence |P_N|=o(N/log N) cannot give a subpower independent absolute cube price. For r=|P|>=1, B_P(N) >=kappa_q N/(r+2)-6*2^(omega(q)+r)sqrt N, kappa_q=(6/pi^2)product_(ell|q)ell/(ell+1); subunit count endpoints use zero with the same error. Polynomial Q gives N^(1-o(1)) positive price.
For psi=sum_m a(m)|m> tensor sum_(d in D_m)a(d)|d>, its partial trace is rho_mm'=a(m)conj(a(m'))min(d_m,d_m'), so rho_m1=a(m)d_m and the signed source is exactly sum_m(C_m/d_m)rho_m1. Spectrum alone loses arithmetic diagonal-gauge information; actual character and common-height examples change the source with unchanged spectrum. This does not assume independent arithmetic phases.
For a frozen profile phi, retain C_m(phi)=sum_(d in D_m)mu(d)chi(d)phi(md) and K_phi(m,m')=sum_(d in D_m intersect D_m')phi(md)conj(phi(m'd)); rho_mm'=a(m)conj(a(m'))K_phi(m,m'). The same readout uses C_m(phi)/K_phi(m,1) only where this overlap is nonzero. For phi(n)=exp(-n/x^b-i(n/x)^k)n^(-it), b>=1,k>0,x>=1,N<=lambda*x,lambda^k<pi, |K_phi(m,1)|>=cos(lambda^k/2)exp(-2lambda)d_m. This is a prefix condition, not a full-tail estimate. A sharp (N/2,N] mask has K_phi(m,1)=0 for m>=2. Positive cube/complement prices do not lower-bound the full signed source.

raw_source_record.statement:
Let e=1 for principal chi and0 otherwise, A(s)=(s-1)^e L(s,chi), and v_j=W(s_j)/L(s_j,chi), using the actual inverse Dirichlet series. If every matrix K_N(i,j)=(B^2-v_i conj(v_j))/(s_i+conj(s_j)-2gamma) is positive semidefinite, then bounded half-plane interpolants and normal-family compactness give F holomorphic on H_gamma with |F|<=B and A(s)F(s)=(s-1)^e W(s). Thus every finite-height zero of L in H_gamma is excluded; the principal point1 is its permitted pole, not a zero. Imprimitive Euler factors/natural zeros remain. This sufficient fixed-weight bounded-reciprocal criterion is not equivalent to qualitative zero exclusion.
Approximate global interpolants with the same B and errors epsilon_N->0 at each fixed sample suffice. For Re s_j>=1+delta, v_j^(J)=W(s_j)sum_(n<=J)mu(n)chi(n)n^(-s_j) has error <=|W(s_j)|J^(-delta)/delta. If Re s_j-gamma>=d>0, |v_j|<=V and sample errors<=r, the finite matrix error norm is <=N(2Vr+r^2)/(2d); a larger least-eigenvalue margin certifies that finite matrix only. Neither one finite PSD matrix, diagonal bounds, a nonzero limiting error nor samples escaping to infinity proves the all-N hypothesis. A finite hidden-pole countermodel is ambient analytic evidence, not an arithmetic counterexample.

raw_source_record.statement:
Put s(r^2)=chi(r)^2 (zero off squares), q1=delta1-p chi(p)delta_p, q2=delta1-p chi(p)^2 delta_(p^2), c_M=q1*(mu chi), c_L=q1*q2*(lambda chi)*s. Then c_L=w*c_M, w=q2*s*s, and c_M=z*c_L, z=q2^(-1)*s^(-1)*s^(-1), s^(-1)(r^2)=mu(r)chi(r)^2. Both square-supported shifts have finite sum |w(d)|d^(-sigma), sum |z(d)|d^(-sigma) for every sigma>1/2.
For any sequence u with sum_(m<=Y)|u(m)|^2<=C Y, the COMPLETE mismatch E_(u,d)(x)=sum_m u(m)[f_x(dm)-f_(x/d)(m)] obeys ||E_(u,d)||_2 <<_(b,k) sqrt(C)[X^(b/2)d^(-1/2)+X^(2-b)d^(b-2)]exp(-c d/X^b), with fixed c>0. Low m<=X/d and the entire high Gram/tail are paid; both actual sources satisfy the square-coefficient hypothesis. Summing every w/z shift gives full errors O(X^theta log^3(2X)), theta=max(b/2,2-b), and bounded forward/inverse shell operators at every sigma>1/2. Hence for gamma>=theta, each j=1,2 separately has ||F_cM||_(j,X)<<_epsilon X^(gamma+epsilon) iff the corresponding full c_L bound holds. Minimum theta is2/3 at b=4/3. This is not L1-to-L2 equivalence or a signed estimate.
Transport of finite cores uses each shifted real scale X/d, its own output cuts, the complete small-scale bank and the actual mismatch above; an unpriced x/d substitution is false. Full Mellin descent has nonlinear remainder holomorphic on Re s>2-b and requires the original fixed sufficient prime bank/nonvanishing numerator. Fixed-character ordinary returns do not establish weighted native-Hecke inputs.

raw_source_record.statement:
L_chi(x,y)=sum_(n<=x,P+(n)<=y)lambda(n)chi(n) satisfies L_chi(x,y)=1-sum_(p<=min(x,y))chi(p)L_chi(x/p,p), with INCLUSIVE p. For any coherent approximation F on the complete finite reachable system define Delta_F(x,y)=F(x,y)-1+sum_(p<=min(x,y))chi(p)F(x/p,p). Finite triangular substitution gives F-L_chi=Delta_F(x,y)+sum_(2<=n<=x,P+(n)<=y)lambda(n)chi(n)Delta_F(x/n,P-(n)). Each n has exactly one nonincreasing prime word including repetitions. Equal descendant states must be merged with their signed coefficients before norm estimation.
At y=x, for a fixed 1/2<gamma<1, the OPEN bound |F(X,X)|+|Delta_F(X,X)|+|sum_(2<=n<=X)lambda(n)chi(n)Delta_F(X/n,P-(n))|<<_epsilon X^(gamma+epsilon), every large real X, implies the full Liouville summatory bound and all-height ordinary zero exclusion through L(2s,chi^2)/L(s,chi). F may vary with the root only if one coherent F defines all defects in that root's system.
For M_chi(x,y)=sum_(n<=x,P+(n)<=y)mu(n)chi(n), L_chi=sum_(r<=sqrt x,P+(r)<=y)chi(r)^2 M_chi(x/r^2,y), and M_chi=sum_(r<=sqrt x,P+(r)<=y)mu(r)chi(r)^2 L_chi(x/r^2,y). Both uniform-in-y weighted sup operators cost at most zeta(2gamma) for gamma>1/2. A root-only bound does not supply a uniform-y bound; finite spectrum or replacing p by p-minus does not pay the defect.

Set u_j=(-1)^j p^(-j(j-1)/2)/C_j, Phi_p(t)=sum_(j>=0)u_j exp(-p^j t), F(x)=sum_n a(n)Phi_p(n/x), F0(x)=sum_n a(n)exp(-n/x). For0<t<=1, log Phi_p(t)<=-(log(1/t))^2/(2log p)+(log(1/t))/2. Signed dilation moments sum_j u_j p^(mj)=0 for every integer m>=0; positive kernel moments do not vanish. Its Mellin multiplier K_p(s)=Gamma(s)product_(j>=0)(1-p^(-(s+j))) is entire and nonzero for Re s>0. The full transform is K_p(s)L(2s,chi^2)/L(s,chi); a full L1 growth bound at gamma>1/2 gives all-height ordinary zero exclusion. Gamma inverse is not polynomial in height.
Exactly F=sum_j u_j F0(x/p^j) and F0=sum_j v_j F(x/p^j), v_j=1/C_j. Forward absolute gamma-sum is finite and inverse cost <=C_p^(-1)/(1-p^(-gamma)), gamma>0, including all shifted shells/small arguments. Thus fixed filtering preserves separate L1/L2 every-epsilon growth exponents. Actual filtered coefficients are sum_(p^j|n)u_j a(n/p^j); every sign/zero remains. Positive absolute price is (phi(q)/q)C_p x+O_(p,q)(1).
For1/2<gamma<1 choose eta>0 small, A>1-gamma+2eta, C^2/(2log p)>1-gamma+2eta. Freeze Y=X exp(-C sqrt(log X)), Z=2AX log X, R=ceil(sqrt(2(1-gamma+2eta)log X/log p)). The full low/high/filter tails have respective bounds X^(1-C^2/(2log p)+o(1)), O(X^(1-A)), O_p(X p^(-(R+1)(R+2)/2)). The resulting finite sum over Y<n<=Z,0<=j<=R returns to F with O(X^(gamma-eta)).
For H=floor(X^gamma), use consecutive blocks of EXACTLY H integers except the last. B_I=sum_(n in I)a(n), V=sum_I B_I Phi_p(min(I)/x) has full error O(X^gamma), J=O(X^(1-gamma)log X), and its full Gram retains every signed cross-block term. The stronger OPEN E=sum_I|B_I|^2<<X^(3gamma-1+epsilon) suffices; its diagonal O(X log X) is paid for gamma>=2/3. No cancellation follows from flatness or block count.

If such a fiber has K prime members, its exact total l1 residual is4|b_m|K/(1+K), squared l2 residual4|b_m|^2 K/(1+K). Since sum|c|<=2(1+1/p)zeta(2)N and sum|c|^2<=8(1+p)zeta(2)^3N, both total residuals are O_p(N/Y). The signed mean is preserved, not estimated. Any |w_n|<=1 has readout error O_p(N/Y); arbitrary masked-subset projections need their own fiber calculation.

A full signed projected bound for a fixed covering prime pair has the ordinary all-height return. Smooth singleton fibers still have exponent-one positive price; none of these residual estimates controls the projected scalar.

Put f(u)=exp(-gamma u)T(exp u), g_d(u)=exp(-gamma u)B(exp(u)/d),d=1,...,D. The complete Gram G_de=<g_d,g_e> is positive definite (b(1)=1); h_d=<g_d,f>. Exactly min_z||f-sum_d z_d g_d||^2=||f||^2-h*G^(-1)h=sup_(y!=0,<g_d,y>=0)|<y,f>|^2/||y||^2. No sector correlation is deleted.
For P_p(z)=1-chi(p)p^(1-z), D_b=P_p L(z,chi), D_t=P_p L(2z,chi^2). If an actual zero rho=beta+i tau has beta>gamma, y_rho(u)=exp(-(conj(rho)-gamma)u) is orthogonal to every g_d, <y_rho,f>=P_p(rho)L(2rho,chi^2)/rho and ||y_rho||^2=1/[2(beta-gamma)]. Hence every D,z has residual >=2(beta-gamma)|P_p(rho)L(2rho,chi^2)/rho|^2. Minima tending to0 for a fixed covering pair of distinct unramified primes (one chi(p)!=1 for nonprincipal chi) exclude all finite-height zeros above gamma; the principal pole is not a false zero signal. Put Q*=Q_p*(delta_1-delta_p), b*=Q* convolved with h, c*=Q* convolved with a. The mean-zero periodic b* has period p^2 q independent of R and b*(0)=0. Its Laplace coefficients B_j and Phi derivatives obey B_j Phi^(j)(0)=0 for every j; hence |sum_l b*(l)Phi(Dl/X)|<< (D/X)^R. For u=(R+gamma)/(R+1), U=V=X^(u/2), M=X^((K-gamma)/(K-1)), the entire T*=sum_(d>U,e>V,del<=M)a(d)a(e)b*(l)Phi(del/X) differs from Z*=sum_n c*(n)Phi(n/X) by O_epsilon(X^(gamma+epsilon)); all short, small-double and infinite-tail terms are included. Its Mellin factor is Gamma((s+delta)/6)exp(-i*pi*(s+delta)/12)/6 times ((2^(s+delta)-1)/(s+delta))^J times (1-chi(p)p^(1-s))(1-p^(-s))/L(s,chi). New factors have no zeros in Re(s)>0. Retain sum_(d>U,e>V,L<del<=M,gcd(d,e)<=G)(lambda chi)(d)(lambda chi)(e)(q1*q2*chi)(l)f_x(del). Its complete complement costs O(X^gamma log^2(2X)) in P_X. At b=3/2 the conditional return extends to gamma=1/2; the Mellin integral is improper signed, not absolutely integrable. For any coefficient sequence with cumulative absolute mass O(Y), changing fixed damping constants has full primitive defect O(X^(2-b)) for k>2 and O(X^(2-b)log X) for k=2. The direct Mellin remainder is holomorphic on positive Re(s)>2-b. At b=2 the DISTINCT source c_mu=Q_p*(mu chi)=(mu chi)*(mu chi)*(Q_p*chi) has the same complete core reduction for 0<gamma<1, with mu(d)mu(e)chi(de), not mu(de). raw_source_record.statement: For fixed tau,sigma>0 and positive integer Q, the finite span of G_tau(log(n/x)), (n,Q)=1, is dense in H_sigma. Under logarithmic conjugation, an orthogonal vector would have an entire Gaussian convolution of order at most two vanishing at all log n-tau sigma with (n,Q)=1; exponential zero count contradicts the quadratic Jensen bound. Hence a finite-bank inverse from G252 remains norm-sharp on finite Gaussian polynomials. Coefficient caps do not change norm ratios after rescaling. Applying C_p=[(I-p chi(p)D_p)(I-p chi(p)^2D_p^2)]/[(I+chi(p)D_p)(I-chi(p)^2D_p^2)] to polynomials supported away from pq and the bank has dense range: numerator zeros are at most a null frequency set. This retains natural zeros and the exact compensating-prime ray law, and bank inversion restores its prime rays. The resulting free-coefficient class lacks the fixed global lambda law. Thus Gaussian regularity and these local recurrences alone cannot improve the uniform inverse norm; additional actual arithmetic structure remains eligible.

Choose a fixed Schwartz eta with Fourier transform 1 there, so F=eta*F. For rho_m(v,w)=c_m^2(1+v^2)^(-m)(1+w^2)^(-m), Cauchy gives ||F(v,w)||^2<=C_m(1+v^2)^m(1+w^2)^m int rho_m||F||^2, without a label-count loss. Conversely a pointwise bound with polynomial degree J gives a finite weighted average for m>J+1/2. Therefore existence of a finite-degree pointwise estimate and of a finite-m weighted-average estimate is equivalent on this fixed-bandwidth class. Weighted Hilbert transport and its exact signed Gram expansion remain valid, but the averaged condition is not an independently weaker arithmetic obligation. Retain all original arithmetic labels, radial weights, both ordered cross terms, masks and Fourier tails.

raw_source_record.statement: For the full G255 coefficients fix integer h>=1,b>1,integer k>bh and f_x(n)=exp(-(n/x^b)^h-i(n/x)^k). With tr(W Gamma)=1, the whole diagonal is C_q K_(b,h)X^b+O(X^(b/2)log^2 X), K_(b,h)=(2^b-1)Gamma(1+1/h)/(b 2^(1/h)). raw_source_record.statement: For a fixed Gaussian log kernel and its eta combination U(x)-2U(x/2), comparison coefficients can retain squareful zeros and agreement with mu on every z-smooth integer, z=log X, while their complete eta energy is large. In the complex multiplicative class, choose small-prime values -1 and large-prime values p^(it). The full x^(1+it) main term has eta factor 1-2^(-it): t=0 is annihilated, t=pi/log2 survives and yields energy at least c X^2/log^4 X with the full error retained. A real squarefree-supported multiplicative H_X assigns prime signs -1 below z and above Y=2exp(3tau)X, and +1 between. Then |H_X|^2=mu^2 and the complete one-large-prime expansion, eta-cancelled base and above-Y^2 Gaussian tail give G_(H_X)(x)<=-cX/log X on [X,2X], hence energy at least c^2 X^2/log^2 X. H_X depends on X; moving-band constants are not uniform fixed-Euler-correction constants. These classes omit the global mu convolution inverse law. The result obstructs uniform estimates for these enlarged classes, not actual mu or one fixed comparison sequence at every scale.
