raw_source_record.statement: For squarefree primorial P let V_t be the augmented oriented-deletion complex on subsets with product<=t, graded by subset cardinality. A window is the relative complex V_b/V_a, with parity trace sum_(a<d<=b,d|P)mu(d), not a divisor-closed interval complex. If P contains2 and3, the interval (P/3,2P/3] contains exactly P/2. Its deletion faces lie below P/3, so the relative complex has one generator, zero differential and nonzero homology. The generator is distance P/6 from each endpoint. Hence universal support in additive endpoint strips o(X) fails for this primorial-window model. The exact least-prime matching instead crosses a full multiplicative layer. The least-prime partner P is outside the interval; no internal elementary face matching can pair the surviving generator. This does not estimate the full signed Mobius source.

raw_source_record.statement: Group identical nonzero row and column profiles of the threshold matrix T_ij=1_(u_i v_j<=N). On its exact d-step staircase, orthonormal class embeddings give T=U B V*, B=diag(sqrt(m_i))L_d diag(sqrt(n_j)), with positive integer multiplicities and L_d the d-by-d lower triangular all-ones matrix. Its singular values are sigma_j(L_d)=[2sin((2j-1)pi/(4d+2))]^(-1). Thus for0<=k<d every rank-k approximation has operator error at least sigma_(k+1)(B)>=sigma_(k+1)(L_d)>=(2d+1)/(pi(2k+1)); the corresponding squared Frobenius error is at least the sum of the squared discarded singular values. Zero/repeated classes are handled before this compression; different partitions can have different d. This sharpens the older1/2 operator floor and preserves exact continuation classes. It is not a lower bound for a fixed actual signed contraction alpha^T(T-R)beta, nor a claim that every partition has growing staircase rank.

raw_source_record.statement: Set ell=log2, beta_1=3/4,beta_2=7/8, h_j(v)=exp(-beta_j v)1_[0,ell)(v). The transform K_j(s)=(exp(ell(s-beta_j))-1)/(s-beta_j) has removable value ell at beta_j and simple zeros beta_j+2pi i k/ell, k!=0. These two zero sets are disjoint. Complete sources F_j(x)=sum_(x<=n<2x)mu(n)chi(n)(n/x)^(-beta_j) satisfy T_j(s)=int F_j(x)x^(-s)dx/x=K_j(s)/L(s,chi) initially Re(s)>1. Complete every-epsilon shell-L1 bounds for BOTH sources at common gamma make both T_j holomorphic above gamma, and local reciprocal germs glue on {K_j!=0}, excluding every finite-height zero with multiplicity. For fixed strip gamma<=sigma<=A, max_j|K_j(s)|>=c/(|Im(s)|+C), c=1-exp(-ell/16), C=1+max_j max(|gamma-beta_j|,|A-beta_j|). There is no height-independent positive lower bound. Fixed m-fold self-convolution preserves disjoint zero sets, gives C^(m-2) kernels for m>=2 and inverse loss of degree m. A common arbitrary mollifier may introduce shared zeros.

raw_source_record.statement: For real z in[-1,1]^I, Az=b and complex weights w, every real y yields Re(exp(-i theta)w) dot z <= b dot y+sum|Re(exp(-i theta)w)-A^T y|. A modulus certificate needs all theta and any full omitted tail. Fix finite primes P and ordinary chi modulo q. Write squarefree n=dr with d dividing product(P), (r,product(P))=1, and set a_z(dr)=mu(d)chi(dr)z_r, z_1=1, a_z=0 on nonsquarefree n. This retains all P-prime laws and natural zeros; actual mu chi is feasible at z_r=mu(r), but rough-factor multiplicativity is omitted. For the COMPLETE finite cumulative source, B_r=chi(r)sum_(d|product(P),dr<=N)mu(d)chi(d), M_z=B_1+sum_(r>1)B_r z_r. Its exact directional support is Re(exp(-i theta)B_1)+sum_(r>1)|Re(exp(-i theta)B_r)|. Terminal squarefree qP-coprime r in(N/2,N] have |B_r|=1. Averaging theta gives sup_z|M_z|>=(2/pi)R_Q(N)=delta_Q N/pi+O_Q(sqrt N), delta_Q=(phi(Q)/Q)product_(p not dividing Q)(1-p^(-2))>0. Thus this exact signed relaxation has linear worst-case price for fixed P,q. Optimizers may depend on N. The result is neither an actual Mobius lower bound nor automatically a Gaussian/nonlinear-source obstruction.

raw_source_record.statement:
For a_n=mu(n)chi(n), I_N={N+1,...,2N}, g_tau(u)=(2*pi*tau)^(-1/2)exp(-u^2/(2*tau)), f_N(t)=sum_(n in I_N)a_n g_tau(t-log n) and E_N=int_R|f_N|^2dt, set kappa=(4*pi*tau)^(-1/2). Exactly E_N=kappa D_N+2*kappa Re sum_(h=1)^(N-1) sum_(n=N+1)^(2N-h)mu(n)mu(n+h)chi(n)conj(chi(n+h))exp(-log(1+h/n)^2/(4*tau)), D_N=sum_(n in I_N)|a_n|^2<=N. This is the full covariance: both orientations, joint n,h weight, endpoints and all squareful/ramified zeros remain. The diagonal is not a lower bound for the signed energy. With all-one bounded coefficients E_N>=kappa exp(-log(2)^2/(4*tau))N^2, and shifts in[N/4,N/2] alone cost order N^2. This rejects absolute sublinear shift truncation for the generic kernel, not actual Mobius cancellation.
For A_N(xi)=sum_(n in I_N)a_n n^(-i xi), Fourier convention exp(-i xi t) gives E_N=(2*pi)^(-1)int_R exp(-tau*xi^2)|A_N(xi)|^2dxi. The ENTIRE |xi|>H complement is <=N^2 exp(-tau H^2)/(2*pi*tau*H), H>0. Fix delta>0 and H_N=sqrt((2-2gamma+delta)log N/tau), N>=2. The complement is O(N^(2gamma-delta)/sqrt(log N)). Thus E_N<<_epsilon N^(2gamma+epsilon) is equivalent to the same every-epsilon bound for int_(-H_N)^(H_N)exp(-tau*xi^2)|A_N(xi)|^2dxi. This is a continuous integral, not a finite sample test. For gamma>1/2 the arithmetic premise is precisely a one-sided upper bound of this order on the entire real signed off-diagonal; separate absolute shift bounds are stronger, not necessary.
For each h retain alpha_h(r)=chi(r)conj(chi(r+h)) and all q Fourier coefficients c_h(b)=q^(-1)sum_(r mod q)alpha_h(r)exp(-2*pi*i*b*r/q); alpha_h(n)=sum_(b mod q)c_h(b)exp(2*pi*i*b*n/q). This exact finite transform supplies no arithmetic estimate. For the quartic character modulo5 with chi(2)=i, alpha_1 on1,2,3,4 is(-i,-1,i,0). The unshifted divisor-Ramanujan span {c_d(n):d|5}, constant on units, cannot represent it. Shifted/richer or infinite expansions are not excluded and owe their own convergence/tails.
Under the stated every-epsilon energy premise, g_(2tau)=g_tau*g_tau and Cauchy-Schwarz bound each FULL width-2tau block source by ||g_tau||_2 sqrt(E_N). Sum all N<=x^(1+eta) geometrically, costing O(x^((1+eta)(gamma+epsilon/2))); sum every N>x^(1+eta) using C_tau N exp(-log(N/x)^2/(4*tau)), whose complete dyadic sum is O_A(x^(-A)) for every A>0 at sufficiently large x. Retain n=1 separately. Choosing eta and epsilon for each requested epsilon'>0 yields F_(2tau)(x)=sum_(n>=1)a_n g_(2tau)(log(n/x))<<x^(gamma+epsilon'). No backward heat inverse or omitted cross-block claim is used; the block premise is sufficient, not asserted necessary.
For x<=1 and any A>1, |F_(2tau)(x)|<=C_A zeta(A)x^A. Initially Re(s)>1, int_0^infinity F_(2tau)(x)x^(-s)dx/x=exp(tau*s^2)/L(s,chi). Both tails and logarithmic derivatives continue this integral holomorphically to Re(s)>gamma. The nonzero multiplier excludes all ordinary L zeros there at every finite height and multiplicity; the principal pole at1 is a reciprocal zero. No height-uniform inverse norm is required. Neither energy nor low-band arithmetic premise has been proved.

raw_source_record.statement:
For fixed real r>0, M(x)=sum_(n<=x)a_n (zero below0), R_r(x)=sum_(n<=x)a_n(x-n)^r/Gamma(r+1), S_r(x)=Gamma(r+1)x^(-r)R_r(x). Retain n=1 and the zero n=x endpoint. Define k_b(t)=t^(b-1)/Gamma(b) for t>0 and zero for t<=0. Causal beta integration gives R_r=k_r*M and k_b*k_c=k_(b+c). For nonnegative phi in C_c^infinity(0,1), integral phi=1, integer m>r and phi_h(t)=h^(-1)phi(t/h), put K_h=k_(m-r)*phi_h^(m). Then K_h*R_r=phi_h*M and ||K_h||_1=C_(r,phi)h^(-r). All endpoint terms vanish; cancellation of the first m moments of phi^(m) gives the complete K_1(u)=O(u^(-r-1)) far tail, including fractional r.
If |R_r(x)|<=C(1+x)^(r+theta),0<=theta<1, and |a_n|<=1, then for1<=h<=x, |M(x)|<<x^(r+theta)h^(-r)+h+1. The discrete variation cost is |M(x)-M(x-u)|<=u+1. Choosing h=x^beta gives M(x)<<x^beta, beta=(r+theta)/(r+1)=1-(1-theta)/(r+1). Every-positive-epsilon source bounds yield the corresponding every-epsilon conclusion. A NEW uniform variation law |M(x)-M(x-u)|<<X^kappa h^alpha for x~X,0<=u<=h,alpha>0,kappa>=0 would give exponent [alpha(r+theta)+r*kappa]/(r+alpha), only when the optimizer h=X^((r+theta-kappa)/(r+alpha)) lies in[1,X]. This extra short-interval hypothesis is not supplied.
The exponent beta is sharp in the class of arbitrary bounded coefficients. Fix integer m>r,B=max_(0<=l<=m)binom(m,l), sufficiently sparse integer T_j (a late tail of2^(2^j) suffices), H_j=floor(T_j^beta). On n=T_j+l H_j+k,0<=l<=m,1<=k<=H_j set b_n=(-1)^l binom(m,l)/B; elsewhere b_n=0. Disjoint complete blocks have mass0 and |b_n|<=1, while M_b(T_j+H_j)=H_j/B. For D(v)=sum_(l=0)^m(-1)^l binom(m,l)(v-l)_+^r, D is bounded everywhere and O(v^(r-m)) for v>m+1. Each block contributes H_j^r/[B Gamma(r+1)]sum_(k=1)^(H_j)D((x-T_j-k)/H_j) to R_r[b](x), hence O(H_j^(r+1)) at EVERY x, including its full fractional far tail. Sparse summation yields R_r[b](x)=O(x^(r+theta)), yet no M_b exponent beta-delta,delta>0, holds. This generic example is not a Mobius/character counterexample or optimality proof for actual arithmetic coefficients.
For the arithmetic specialization a_n=mu(n)chi(n), the previously recorded fixed-Riesz principle local:G134 avoids this loss for zero exclusion: a fixed-r S_r(x)<<_epsilon x^(theta+epsilon) gives int_1^infinity S_r(x)x^(-s)dx/x=Gamma(s)Gamma(r+1)/(Gamma(s+r+1)L(s,chi)), initially Re(s)>1. The majorant B(Re(s),r+1)sum_n n^(-Re(s)) pays Fubini; S_r vanishes below1. The multiplier is holomorphic and nonzero for Re(s)>0, so compact epsilon margins give all-finite-height, all-multiplicity zero exclusion in Re(s)>theta. Principal poles and imprimitive/natural zeros remain literal. Direct c=1-theta contrasts with c=(1-theta)/(r+1) through unsmoothed recovery. statement:
For fixed real r>0, M(x)=sum_(n<=x)a_n (zero below0), R_r(x)=sum_(n<=x)a_n(x-n)^r/Gamma(r+1), S_r(x)=Gamma(r+1)x^(-r)R_r(x). Retain n=1 and the zero n=x endpoint. Define k_b(t)=t^(b-1)/Gamma(b) for t>0 and zero for t<=0. Causal beta integration gives R_r=k_r*M and k_b*k_c=k_(b+c). For nonnegative phi in C_c^infinity(0,1), integral phi=1, integer m>r and phi_h(t)=h^(-1)phi(t/h), put K_h=k_(m-r)*phi_h^(m). Then K_h*R_r=phi_h*M and ||K_h||_1=C_(r,phi)h^(-r). All endpoint terms vanish; cancellation of the first m moments of phi^(m) gives the complete K_1(u)=O(u^(-r-1)) far tail, including fractional r.
If |R_r(x)|<=C(1+x)^(r+theta),0<=theta<1, and |a_n|<=1, then for1<=h<=x, |M(x)|<<x^(r+theta)h^(-r)+h+1. The discrete variation cost is |M(x)-M(x-u)|<=u+1. Choosing h=x^beta gives M(x)<<x^beta, beta=(r+theta)/(r+1)=1-(1-theta)/(r+1). Every-positive-epsilon source bounds yield the corresponding every-epsilon conclusion. A NEW uniform variation law |M(x)-M(x-u)|<<X^kappa h^alpha for x~X,0<=u<=h,alpha>0,kappa>=0 would give exponent [alpha(r+theta)+r*kappa]/(r+alpha), only when the optimizer h=X^((r+theta-kappa)/(r+alpha)) lies in[1,X]. This extra short-interval hypothesis is not supplied.
The exponent beta is sharp in the class of arbitrary bounded coefficients. Fix integer m>r,B=max_(0<=l<=m)binom(m,l), sufficiently sparse integer T_j (a late tail of2^(2^j) suffices), H_j=floor(T_j^beta). On n=T_j+l H_j+k,0<=l<=m,1<=k<=H_j set b_n=(-1)^l binom(m,l)/B; elsewhere b_n=0. Disjoint complete blocks have mass0 and |b_n|<=1, while M_b(T_j+H_j)=H_j/B. For D(v)=sum_(l=0)^m(-1)^l binom(m,l)(v-l)_+^r, D is bounded everywhere and O(v^(r-m)) for v>m+1. Each block contributes H_j^r/[B Gamma(r+1)]sum_(k=1)^(H_j)D((x-T_j-k)/H_j) to R_r[b](x), hence O(H_j^(r+1)) at EVERY x, including its full fractional far tail. Sparse summation yields R_r[b](x)=O(x^(r+theta)), yet no M_b exponent beta-delta,delta>0, holds. This generic example is not a Mobius/character counterexample or optimality proof for actual arithmetic coefficients.
For the arithmetic specialization a_n=mu(n)chi(n), the previously recorded fixed-Riesz principle local:G134 avoids this loss for zero exclusion: a fixed-r S_r(x)<<_epsilon x^(theta+epsilon) gives int_1^infinity S_r(x)x^(-s)dx/x=Gamma(s)Gamma(r+1)/(Gamma(s+r+1)L(s,chi)), initially Re(s)>1. The majorant B(Re(s),r+1)sum_n n^(-Re(s)) pays Fubini; S_r vanishes below1. The multiplier is holomorphic and nonzero for Re(s)>0, so compact epsilon margins give all-finite-height, all-multiplicity zero exclusion in Re(s)>theta. Principal poles and imprimitive/natural zeros remain literal. Direct c=1-theta contrasts with c=(1-theta)/(r+1) through unsmoothed recovery. hypotheses.complete_windows: For real X>=2 and integer 1<=H<=X, B_H(k)=sum_{0<=j<H}m(k-j), k>=1; A_H(x)=sum_{0<=j<H}e^(-j/x); E_chi(X,H)=H^(-1)sum_{k>=1}|B_H(k)|^2e^(-k/(2X)). Every overlap, initial partial window and infinite damped tail is included.
hypotheses.diagonal: D_chi(X,H)=A_H(2X)/H sum_{n>=1}mu(n)^2 1_{(n,q)=1}e^(-n/(2X)); O_chi=E_chi-D_chi is the complete real signed off-diagonal, with both lag orientations and potentially negative sign.

hypotheses.target_regime: For the diagonal-paid route fix 1/2<gamma<1 and 0<theta<1 with theta>=2(1-gamma), and take H=floor(X^theta). The inequality theta>=2(1-gamma), together with theta<1, forces gamma>1/2.

quantifier_scope.exact_identity: The identities hold for every integer 1<=H<=X and all x in [X,2X]. The target asks for every epsilon>0 on every sufficiently large shell, with fixed q,chi,gamma,theta before the shell.

raw_source_record.statement:
Fix a(n)=mu(n)chi(n), M(x)=sum_(n<=x)a(n), M(x)=0 for x<1, and 1/2<gamma<1. Put f(y)=exp(-gamma y)M(exp y) for y>=0 and zero otherwise; E(Y)=int_0^Y|f|^2, A(Y)=int_0^Y y|f|^2, C_f(h;Y)=int_h^Y conjugate(f(y))f(y-h)dy. Define P(Y)=Re sum_(p<=exp Y)log(p)chi(p)p^-gamma C_f(log p;Y); Q is the complete analogous sum over p^j<=exp Y,j>=2 with chi(p)^j p^(-j gamma). The exact coefficient identity a log=-a*(Lambda chi) gives A+P+Q=Re int conjugate(f)J_gamma f, J_gamma f(y)=int_0^y exp(-gamma(y-v))f(v)dv. All finite endpoints, repeated powers and ramified/squareful zeros remain. Cauchy and causal shift contraction give |Q|<=C_gamma E, C_gamma=sum_p log(p)p^(-2gamma)/(1-p^-gamma)<infinity. Writing g=J_gamma f gives Re int conjugate(f)g=|g(Y)|^2/2+gamma int|g|^2 in [0,E/gamma]. Therefore -C_gamma E<=A+P<=(1/gamma+C_gamma)E; the upper coefficient is <12 when gamma>=3/4.
For fixed delta>0,C>=0 and an unbounded sequence Y_k, the actual-source premise P(Y_k)>=-(1-delta)A(Y_k)-C E(Y_k) implies A(Y_k)<=B E(Y_k), B=(1/gamma+C_gamma+C)/delta. For Y_k>=2B, positivity gives E(Y_k)<=2E(2B), so monotonicity pays all intervening scales and E(infinity)<=2E(2B)<=[exp(4(1-gamma)B)-1]/(1-gamma); also A(infinity)<=2B E(2B). Conversely A(infinity)<infinity implies that premise for any fixed delta>0 and a sufficiently large fixed C. Thus the existential sparse criterion is equivalent to finite logarithmically weighted energy, not a weaker analytic assumption.
If E(infinity)<infinity, F(s)=s int_0^infinity exp(-(s-gamma)y)f(y)dy is holomorphic for Re(s)>gamma and initially equals 1/L(s,chi); |F(s)|<=|s|sqrt(E(infinity)/(2(Re(s)-gamma))). Continuing LF=1 excludes every zero there, while the principal pole is a reciprocal zero. A hypothetical zero with real part >gamma therefore forces E to diverge, A/E to infinity and P/A to -1. No converse from that limit to a zero is asserted.
A universal lower bound P_f>=-(1-delta)A_f-C E_f for arbitrary f is false. The test f_t=exp(ity)1_[0,Y] and a finite nonnegative prime-frequency product have weighted mean P_f<=-(Y/4)sum_(p<=exp(Y/2),p not dividing q)log(p)p^-gamma. This defeats fixed delta,C as Y grows. Y and the finite prime set are fixed before the height average. This comparison is not an arithmetic counterexample. The full logarithmic identity and finite-prime method retain their earlier credit; the contribution is the precise complete energy criterion and sparse cumulative equivalence.

raw_source_record.statement:
For a fixed integer r>=2 and ordinary chi, define b_r(n)=chi(n)sum_(d^r|n)mu(n/d^r), B_r(x)=sum_(n<=x)b_r(n), and M(x)=sum_(n<=x)mu(n)chi(n), both zero below 1. The local factor is (1-z)/(1-z^r), z=chi(p)p^-s, hence sum b_r(n)n^-s=L(rs,chi^r)/L(s,chi) initially Re(s)>1. At r=2, b_r=lambda chi; on squarefree n every r has b_r=mu chi. There is no coprimality restriction between d and its cofactor.
Exactly B_r(x)=sum_(d^r<=x)chi(d)^r M(x/d^r) and M(x)=sum_(d^r<=x)mu(d)chi(d)^r B_r(x/d^r). For gamma>1/r set f=e^-gamma y M(e^y), f_r=e^-gamma y B_r(e^y), each zero for y<0, and Z_q(t)=sum_((d,q)=1)d^-t. On every finite [0,Y], ||f_r||_2<=Z_q(r gamma)||f||_2 and ||f||_2<=[Z_q(r gamma)/Z_q(2r gamma)]||f_r||_2. These use summable complete causal shifts; terms beyond e^y vanish exactly. Monotone limits preserve both inequalities, even for infinite norms. Thus the weighted L2 convergence frontiers agree in this range; each constant is <=3 for gamma>=3/4. The numerator is holomorphic and nonzero above 1/r, so one fixed numerator suffices for the zero-return and the proposed two-numerator firewall is unnecessary.
In the logarithmic recurrence the p^j coefficient is -1+r*1_(r divides j). For gamma>1/2 the complete absolute repeated-power price is C_gamma+(r-2)sum_p log(p)p^(-r gamma)/(1-p^(-r gamma)), with C_gamma=sum_p log(p)p^(-2gamma)/(1-p^-gamma). It equals C_gamma at r=2 and is no smaller for r>2; the leading prime term is unchanged. This is a fixed cumulative log-L2 adaptation of classical square-divisor/Liouville identities, not a new generic transform or a free exponent gain.

raw_source_record.statement:
For squarefree n<=N, the ordered-distinct-prime word fibre has m_n=omega(n)! members, with one empty word at1. The summing pushdown P has PP*=diag(m_n), ||P||^2=max m_n and min_(Pz=a)||z||^2=sum|a_n|^2/m_n. Fibre averaging is an orthogonal projection but is not P; normalizing P by m_n^-1/2 restores the ordinary integer lift norm. Max sqrt(omega(n)!)=N^(1/2-o(1)), with exact upper bound sqrt N, by elementary primorial bounds.
For arbitrary positive word weights v_w let beta_n=sum_(w in fibre n)1/v_w, E_v(a)=sum|a_n|^2/beta_n and L_v(H_x)^2=sum beta_n|H_x(n)|^2. Then E_v(a)L_v(H_x)^2>=(sum|a_n H_x(n)|)^2. Take a_n=mu(n) on squarefree integers and H_x(n)=g_tau(log(n/x))-2g_tau(log(2n/x)), tau>0 fixed. This is exactly the complete eta detector with A(n)=mu(n)-2*1_(2|n)mu(n/2), including A(4)=2. H has unique zero in v=log(n/x) at v0=tau-(log2)/2 and a positive minimum on[v0+1,v0+2]. Squarefree counting Q(y)=y/zeta(2)+O(sqrt y) makes sum|mu(n)H_x(n)|>=c_tau x for every sufficiently large x when the retained support contains that complete proportional interval. For a bank containing these intervals throughout[X,2X], the integrated diagonal certificate is >=c'_tau X^2, even with pointwise weights (with E inside the integral). Shell-fixed weights allow E outside. This lower-bounds the numerical certificate, not the actual signed detector.
A proposed bounded-order repair also has a complete return. Fix 0<lambda<1, N=floor(2X exp(K0 sqrt(log X))), K=floor(lambda log X/loglog X). All n>N eta tails are O(X^-D) for sufficiently large fixed K0. For s=1+1/log N,r>=1, #{n<=N:squarefree,omega(n)>K}<=e N r^-K(1+log N)^r. Taking r=K/log(1+log N) gives X^(1-lambda+o(1)), paying the entire high-order source with |H|<=3g_tau(0). If a full unweighted low-order word lift had norm <=X^(w+o(1)), then uniformly on[X,2X], |G_tau(x)|<=X^(w+1/2+lambda/2+o(1))+X^(1-lambda+o(1))+O(X^-D). Endpoint exponent Gamma in(0,1) is reached by lambda>=1-Gamma and w<=Gamma-1/2-lambda/2; some such lambda exists iff w<=3Gamma/2-1. Strict versions give strict gains.
That UNWEIGHTED premise is false for every Gamma<1: all primes<=N remain one-word fibres, so ||z||^2>=pi(N)>>N/log N=X^(1-o(1)), forcing w>=1/2. Weighted diagonal renormalizations retain the earlier certificate floor. Signed cross-integer or non-diagonal readouts are not excluded. Generic fibre duality is inherited from the existing word-space components; the increment is the actual eta source, complete growing-order complement and retained-prime failure.

Fix integer k>=1 and K_j(y)=y^j exp(-y-i y^k), 0<=j<k. For F(s)=int_0^infinity y^(s-1)exp(-y-i y^k)dy, the k values F(s),...,F(s+k-1) have no common zero on Re(s)>0. Absolute compact domination gives holomorphy; integrating the derivative of y^s exp(-y-i y^k) gives sF(s)=F(s+1)+ikF(s+k). For k>=2, k consecutive zeros propagate to all F(s+m); for k=1 use the nonzero coefficient 1+i. At fixed s the finite complex measure y^(s-1)exp(-y-i y^k)dy has an analytic Laplace transform on Re(z)>-1. All derivatives zero would make it identically zero. Its pushforward by u=exp(-y) on[0,1] then has all polynomial moments zero and is zero by polynomial density, contradicting its nonzero density. No saddle approximation or formal moment argument is used.
The same conclusion holds for d companions when exp(-y-i y^k) is replaced by exp(-a y-iP(y)), a>0 fixed and P a real polynomial of degree d>=1 with nonzero leading coefficient: sF(s)=aF(s+1)+i sum_(ell=1)^d ell c_ell F(s+ell). For d=1 the coefficient a+ic_1 is nonzero. Arbitrary complex polynomial phases are outside this contract.
For a(n)=mu(n)chi(n), any fixed ordinary chi, let S_j(x)=sum_(n>=1)a(n)K_j(n/x). All sums converge absolutely and locally uniformly, and S_j(x)=O_j(exp(-1/(2x))) as x tends to0 in the basic kernel. On Re(s)>1, complete absolute Fubini gives int_0^infinity S_j(x)x^-s dx/x=F(s+j)/L(s,chi). If, for one common0<gamma<1, every epsilon>0 and every sufficiently large dyadic X, sum_j int_X^(2X)|S_j|dx/x <<_(chi,k,epsilon)X^(gamma+epsilon), all transforms continue holomorphically above gamma. A zero of L of any multiplicity would force all companion values to vanish. Principal poles are handled meromorphically; character and squareful zeros, n=1 and both tails remain. Complete L2 shell bounds at that exponent suffice by Cauchy-Schwarz.
This is a finite-bank source adapter, not an arithmetic estimate or a height-uniform inverse-multiplier theorem. Kernel parameters and all companions must stay fixed; a moving k, selected subbank, coefficient mask, finite cutoff, or exp(-n/x^b-i(n/x)^k) with b!=1 needs a new paid comparison. Earlier finite detector banks retain their credit; the consecutive-moment recurrence is the distinct scoped mechanism.

raw_source_record.statement:
Let V_X be all squarefree q-units n<=X, including1, and orient every edge e=(n,pn) with p not dividing nq and pn<=X. This graph is connected. Put B_e=delta_n-delta_(pn), (B_chi)_e=delta_n-chi(p)delta_(pn), a(n)=mu(n)chi(n). If a=B_chi F+r then for every complex test w, sum a(n)w(n)=sum r(n)w(n)+sum_e F_e[w(n)-chi(p)w(pn)]. This is bilinear; no conjugated character is inserted. For any positive c_e, the flow term is bounded by (sum|F_e|^2/c_e)^(1/2)(sum c_e|w(n)-chi(p)w(pn)|^2)^(1/2), with the complete residual also retained.
The vertex gauge U_nn=chi(n) and edge gauge V_ee=chi(n) at the lower endpoint are unitary, and B_chi=U B V^-1, U^-1 a=mu. Thus phase incidence has the ordinary incidence singular spectrum, also with unchanged positive conductances. For any finite target b, inf_(b=BF+r)||r||_1=|sum b|: summing proves the lower bound, and a root residual plus a spanning-tree flow attains it. Therefore inf_(a=B_chi F+r)||r||_1=|sum_(V_X)mu(n)|, independent of chi for fixed q. This equals the principal-character charge, not every nonprincipal M_chi. At w=1 the missing phase response is explicitly M_chi(X)=sum r(n)+sum_e(1-chi(p))F_e.
Every unramified prime p in(X/2,X] is an actual leaf attached to1. If their count L_X>0, its equation gives |F_(1,p)|>=1-|r(p)|. Hence sum|F_e|^2>=(L_X-||r||_1)_+^2/L_X; for arbitrary conductances the energy sum|F_e|^2/c_e is at least (L_X-||r||_1)_+^2/(sum_leaf c_e). The corresponding response factor still must be paid. A prime star has positive gap1 when L_X>=2 and parity sum1-L_X, disproving a generic gap-to-small-charge inference, not the full arithmetic summatory estimate.
For K_j(y)=y^j exp(-y-i y^k), x in[X,2X], fixed j,k, and N=floor(A X log X), the full omitted n>N source tail is O_(A,j)(X^(1-A/2)(log X)^j). Fixed A>2(1-gamma), with positive slack, pays it below exponent gamma. The finite graph then still owes every retained signed response/residual and every companion norm. Earlier neutral-prime boundary and harmonic-index results retain their credit; this record isolates the exact incidence gauge, residual optimum and leaf fee.

raw_source_record.statement:
For a(n)=mu(n)chi(n), M(x)=sum_(n<=x)a(n) and1/2<gamma<1, fix0<kappa<1/(1-gamma), D(X)=max(2,floor((log X)^kappa)). Define P_long(X)=sum_(D(X)<p<=X,p prime)log(p)chi(p)M(X/p). Then P_long(X)=O(X^gamma log X) for all sufficiently large real X is equivalent at the exponent level to M(X)=O(X^gamma).
Use the complete identity M(X)log X=int_1^X M(t)dt/t-sum_(p^j<=X,j>=1)log(p)chi(p)^j M(X/p^j). For finite Y put Q(Y)=sup_(1<=t<=Y)|M(t)|/t^gamma, finite without cancellation. The integral, all p<=D(X), and every j>=2 cost Q(Y)X^gamma[1/gamma+S_gamma(D(X))+C_pp(gamma)], where S_gamma(D)<=C_gamma D^(1-gamma)log(eD) and C_pp(gamma)=sum_(p,j>=2)log(p)p^(-j gamma)<infinity. Dividing by X^gamma log X makes this bracket o(1). Choose one fixed T so its ratio is <=1/2 and the P_long premise holds for all X>=T. Then Q(Y)<=max(Q(T),C+Q(Y)/2), hence Q(Y)<=max(Q(T),2C) uniformly in Y. The converse follows from the same exact identity and complete fees.
The source unit, equality p=D(X), every repeated prime power, m=1 and every unbalanced pair pm<=X are retained; no extra p-free screen is imposed. The finite-horizon norm avoids assuming the desired infinite bound during absorption. At gamma=1/2 this complete absolute prime-power fee diverges, so no boundary result follows. Every-positive-epsilon versions also imply zero exclusion above gamma by applying absorption at gamma+epsilon with a compact horizontal margin. Abel continuation of s int_1^infinity M(x)x^(-s-1)dx=1/L(s,chi) pays all finite heights and multiplicities, with the principal pole retained.
The full Lambda equivalence is already in G135 and the summable higher-power fee plus growing small-prime payment is in G173 in a different Gaussian energy norm. This is their direct pointwise localization/corollary with an explicit subcritical polylogarithmic mask, not a new logarithmic identity, general absorption principle or weaker arithmetic hypothesis. No signed tail estimate has been proved; different masks and norms cannot be exchanged without a complete comparison.

raw_source_record.statement:
For an ordinary chi modulo q, let A_chi(t)=sum_(n<=t)chi(n)=kappa_chi t+B(t), |B(t)|<=q, with kappa_chi=0 if nonprincipal and phi(q)/q if principal. For0<theta<=1, h_theta(x)=A_chi(theta/x)-theta A_chi(1/x) is supported in(0,1], bounded by2q and has Mellin transform int_0^1 h_theta(x)x^(s-1)dx=(theta^s-theta)L(s,chi)/s on Re(s)>0, with the principal singularity at1 removable. The linear mean terms cancel explicitly.
In H_gamma=L2((0,1),x^(2gamma-1)dx),0<gamma<1, evaluation E_rho(f)=int_0^1 f(x)x^(rho-1)dx has norm [2(Re(rho)-gamma)]^-1/2 when Re(rho)>gamma. An L-zero rho annihilates every h_theta, while E_rho(1)=1/rho. Thus for any finite r=1-sum_j c_j h_(theta_j), ||r||^2>=2(Re(rho)-gamma)/|rho|^2. A sequence of COMPLETE residual norms tending to0 excludes all zeros above gamma. No converse density theorem is claimed.
A finite squared norm below2delta/(1+T^2) excludes only the box gamma+delta<=Re(rho)<=1, |Im(rho)|<=T. For any eta in(0,1) the entire omitted interval has cost int_0^eta |r|^2 x^(2gamma-1)dx <=(1+2q sum|c_j|)^2 eta^(2gamma)/(2gamma). Coefficient growth therefore cannot be dropped. One finite positive residual does not establish all-height exclusion or an improving sequence.
For q=1 and theta=1/n, h_theta=-f_n where f_n={1/(nx)}-(1/n){1/x}. This weighted evaluation-functional sufficient criterion already belongs to F08 and the earlier weighted-approximation source. The scoped increment is the ordinary-character formulation with its explicit principal mean correction, finite-box normalization and coefficient-dependent complete tail. No new arithmetic approximation sequence or endpoint follows.

hypotheses.compact_domain: Choose a whole compact K in Re(s)>0 before a hypothetical zero, with Re(s)>=gamma>0 and |s|<=H. For principal chi the compact avoids s=1 and the explicit pole contribution is retained.
hypotheses.sharp_mobius_source: a_d=mu(d)chi(d), P_D(s)=sum_{d<=D}a_d d^(-s), A(y)=sum_{n<=y}chi(n), zero for y<1; R_D(y)=sum_{d<=D}a_d A(y/d)-1 for y>=1. This uses the sharp cutoff, not an arbitrary smooth replacement.

mathematical_status: Written identities, scoped obstruction and conditional return accepted at the stated ordinary-character scope; the required arithmetic estimate remains open.

quantifier_scope.all_heights: For a half-plane result choose a predetermined exhaustion K_j of Re(s)>gamma, excluding the principal pole. Establish a complete strict residual bound on every K_j. Coefficients, D_j, Y_j and constants may depend on fixed chi and K_j, but cannot be selected after choosing an offending zero.
quantifier_scope.family: A conclusion for every ordinary character requires one common gamma across the family; constants may depend on each fixed character/domain. All finite heights and multiplicities are covered by compact exhaustion, not by a finite height sample.
quantifier_scope.finite_choice: The absolute obstruction holds for every finite support and every complex coefficient choice, even source-adapted choices. Signed norms, convergent infinite filters and compact-domain certificates are not excluded.

quantitative_returns.absolute_failure: If b_1=0 then ||r||_sigma>=1. If b_1!=0, every prime p>D with p not dividing q has |r(p)|=|b_1|, so ||r||_sigma=infinity for sigma<=1. For normalized b_1=1, the author also has c(1+kQ)=1 for Q=q*lcm(1,...,D), k>=1.
quantitative_returns.benchmark: Current conditional source-relative c11 remains unchanged; the delivered baseline is not reproved here.
quantitative_returns.direct_finite_certificate: For arbitrary finite A_0(s), nonprincipal L_Y=sum_{n<=Y}chi(n)n^(-s), the whole compact condition sup_K[|1-A_0 L_Y|+|A_0|q(1+H/gamma)Y^(-gamma)]<1 is sufficient. In the principal case replace L_Y by L_Y+kappa Y^(1-s)/(s-1) and retain the same bounded-source remainder price.
quantitative_returns.nonprincipal_identity: R_D(y)=0 for 1<=y<=D. For Re(s)>0, L(s,chi)P_D(s)-1=s integral_D^infinity R_D(y)y^(-s-1)dy. |R_D|<=1+qD; the whole tail beyond Y>=D costs |s|(1+qD)Y^(-Re(s))/Re(s).
quantitative_returns.periodic_tail: For the bounded source G=R_D (nonprincipal) or G=S_D-1 (principal), extended using the same finite sums to y>=0, let Q=q*lcm(1,...,D), C=1+qD, mean gbar, and H_G(y)=integral_0^y(G-gbar), with ||H_G||<=2QC. The tail is gbar Y^(-s)-s H_G(Y)Y^(-s-1)+s(s+1)integral_Y^infinity H_G(y)y^(-s-2)dy; the last term costs |s(s+1)|2QC Y^(-Re(s)-1)/(Re(s)+1). Both boundary terms and the possibly huge Q remain.
quantitative_returns.principal_identity: For kappa=phi(q)/q, A(y)=kappa y+B(y), |B|<=q, and S_D(y)=sum_{d<=D}a_d B(y/d), LP_D-1=kappa s P_D(1)D^(1-s)/(s-1)+s integral_D^infinity[S_D(y)-1]y^(-s-1)dy. The first term is paid in full; the principal pole is not a zero.
quantitative_returns.right_halfplane_scope: For sigma>1 the complete chi and mu chi series belong to the absolute convolution algebra; truncations approximate the inverse in that norm. The obstruction is to crossing the absolute-convergence boundary by finite coefficients, not to all inverse methods.
quantitative_returns.signed_algebra_escape: In a unital submultiplicative Banach algebra of holomorphic functions with continuous point evaluations, ||1-LA_0||<=eta<1 gives inverse A_0 sum_{k>=0}(1-LA_0)^k. The truncated tail is <=||A_0||eta^(K+1)/(1-eta). This is conditional on the complete algebra norm bound.

hypotheses.arithmetic_premise: For one fixed 0<gamma<1 and every epsilon>0, E_a(2^j)<<_(chi,a,epsilon)(2^j)^(2gamma+epsilon) for all large j. A family result requires a common gamma, while fixed-character constants are allowed.
hypotheses.fixed_parameter: Fix a>0 before N and any hypothetical zero. Heat h_t on the whole real line has Fourier multiplier exp(-t xi^2), with hat(nu_N)(xi)=sum_{n<=N}a_n n^(-i xi). The readout squared norm is ||f||_(H1_a)^2=integral_R(|f prime|^2+a^2|f|^2).
hypotheses.source: Fix ordinary chi modulo q; a_n=mu(n)chi(n), nu_N=sum_{n<=N}a_n delta_(log n). Keep squareful/nonunit zero entries literally.

mathematical_status: Written identities, scoped obstruction and conditional return accepted at the stated ordinary-character scope; the required arithmetic estimate remains open.

quantifier_scope.complete_energy: Integrate all t>0 and all real x,xi. The integrable t=0 singularity and low-frequency neighborhood are not omitted.
quantifier_scope.dyadic_return: Only the positive integral part of the weighted-prefix identity is monotone. No monotonicity of the complete E_a(N), unsmoothed partial-block estimate or signed-subset ordering is assumed.
quantifier_scope.height_return: Normal convergence holds on every compact in Re(s)>gamma, including all fixed logarithmic derivatives. All finite heights and multiplicities are retained; principal poles become reciprocal zeros.

quantitative_returns.benchmark: Current conditional source-relative c11 remains unchanged; the delivered baseline is not reproved here.
quantitative_returns.coarse_price: 0<=E_1(N)<=N(N+1)/4 by the bounded-coefficient positive comparison, while D_N/2<=N/2. This is an upper bound, not an arithmetic lower bound on actual energy.
quantitative_returns.complex_diagonal: For a=1, E_1(N)=D_N/2+Re sum_{m<n}a_m conjugate(a_n)m/n, D_N=sum_{n<=N}|a_n|^2. The inner complex sum is not itself asserted real. For gamma>1/2 the diagonal is separately paid.
quantitative_returns.finite_site_readout: For actual nonzero sites u_1<...<u_m, the exact minimum squared H1_a norm with f(u_i)=1 is C_a=2a[1+sum_{i<m}tanh(a(u_(i+1)-u_i)/2)]<=2a+a^2(u_m-u_1), and |M|^2<=C_a E_a. Empty support has M=E=0. Both exterior tails are included.
quantitative_returns.green_identity: E_a(N)=2 integral_0^infinity exp(-2a^2 t)||h_t*nu_N||_2^2 dt=(1/(2pi))integral_R|hat(nu_N)(xi)|^2/(a^2+xi^2) dxi=(1/(2a))sum_{m,n<=N}a_m conjugate(a_n)(min(m,n)/max(m,n))^a.
quantitative_returns.interval_readout: |M_chi(N)|^2<=(a^2 log N+2a)E_a(N), the minimum extension cost for f=1 on the whole interval [0,log N].
quantitative_returns.ordinary_return: Under HEAT, F(s)=(s+a)integral_1^infinity B_a(x)x^(-s-a-1)dx converges normally for Re(s)>gamma. Initially F=1/L on Re(s)>1; continuation of LF=1 excludes regular zeros throughout Re(s)>gamma. Natural imprimitive factors remain.
quantitative_returns.weighted_prefix: With B_a(x)=sum_{n<=x}a_n n^a, E_a(N)=integral_1^N |B_a(x)|^2 x^(-2a-1)dx+|B_a(N)|^2/(2a N^(2a)). The terminal exterior term is essential.

hypotheses.entropy: J_X=log 2-H(U|R)=sum_r p_r d(b_r), d(b)=((1+b)/2)log(1+b)+((1-b)/2)log(1-b), with 0 log 0=0. Entropies use natural logarithms.
hypotheses.residue_data: For unit r, N_r=#{n in S_X:n=r mod q}, M_r=sum_{n<=X,n=r mod q}mu(n), p_r=N_r/S, b_r=M_r/N_r when N_r>0.
hypotheses.sample: Fix any positive modulus q. For large X let S_X={n<=X:mu(n)^2=1,(n,q)=1}, S=|S_X|>0, and sample n uniformly. Put U=mu(n) in {+1,-1}, R=n mod q. The algebra holds for arbitrary q; squarefree q only makes the chosen prime-coordinate CRT presentation immediate.

mathematical_status: Written identities, scoped obstruction and conditional return accepted at the stated ordinary-character scope; the required arithmetic estimate remains open.

quantifier_scope.family: ENT means J_X<<_(q,epsilon)X^(-2c+epsilon) for every epsilon>0 and all sufficiently large X. A result for all ordinary characters requires this for every fixed q with one common c; constants may depend on fixed q.
quantifier_scope.scope_of_equivalence: The equivalence is for all characters of a fixed modulus, not for a single chosen character and not for residue entropy alone.
quantifier_scope.zeros_and_tails: Squarefree and conductor exclusions define the actual probability law; no independent sign model replaces it. The ordinary-L return keeps full Abel tails, principal poles, imprimitive factors and all finite heights.

quantitative_returns.actual_residue_counterexample: For q=3,X=2, the squarefree units 1,2 have uniform residues, U=(1,-1) and quadratic chi=(1,-1), so correlation is 1 despite maximal residue entropy. This disproves a residues-only implication, not an asymptotic Mobius bound.
quantitative_returns.benchmark: Current conditional source-relative c11 remains unchanged; the delivered baseline is not reproved here.
quantitative_returns.correlation: M_chi(X)/S=E[U chi(R)]=sum_r p_r b_r chi(r). For |b|<=1, b^2/2<=d(b)<=(log 2)b^2, hence |M_chi(X)|^2<=2 S^2 J_X.
quantitative_returns.equivalence: For fixed q, J_X is comparable to X^(-2)sum_r|M_r|^2 for large X. Character orthogonality gives sum_{chi mod q}|M_chi(X)|^2=phi(q)sum_r|M_r|^2. ENT is therefore equivalent at every-epsilon exponent level to all fixed-q bounds |M_chi(X)|<<X^(1-c+epsilon).
quantitative_returns.joint_divergence: The full divergence from independent uniform sign and Haar residue is exactly J_X+D(P_R||Haar). The elementary bound is at most log 2+O_q(X^(-1)); the parity term may remain of order one.
quantitative_returns.ordinary_return: Under ENT, normal Abel continuation of s integral_1^infinity M_chi(x)x^(-s-1)dx gives 1/L(s,chi) and excludes regular zeros in Re(s)>1-c, with the principal pole handled as a reciprocal zero.
quantitative_returns.paid_residues: N_r=(X/q)C_q+O_q(sqrt X), C_q=product_{p not dividing q}(1-p^(-2))>0. Thus S=(phi(q)/q)C_q X+O_q(sqrt X) and p_r=1/phi(q)+O_q(X^(-1/2)). D(P_R||Haar)=O_q(X^(-1)), including marginal and CRT dependence costs.

hypotheses.residue_data: For unit r, N_r=#{n in S_X:n=r mod q}, M_r=sum_{n<=X,n=r mod q}mu(n), p_r=N_r/S, b_r=M_r/N_r when N_r>0.
hypotheses.sample: Fix any positive modulus q. For large X let S_X={n<=X:mu(n)^2=1,(n,q)=1}, S=|S_X|>0, and sample n uniformly. Put U=mu(n) in {+1,-1}, R=n mod q. The algebra holds for arbitrary q; squarefree q only makes the chosen prime-coordinate CRT presentation immediate.

quantitative_returns.actual_residue_counterexample: For q=3,X=2, the squarefree units 1,2 have uniform residues, U=(1,-1) and quadratic chi=(1,-1), so correlation is 1 despite maximal residue entropy. This disproves a residues-only implication, not an asymptotic Mobius bound.

quantitative_returns.correlation: M_chi(X)/S=E[U chi(R)]=sum_r p_r b_r chi(r). For |b|<=1, b^2/2<=d(b)<=(log 2)b^2, hence |M_chi(X)|^2<=2 S^2 J_X.
quantitative_returns.equivalence: For fixed q, J_X is comparable to X^(-2)sum_r|M_r|^2 for large X. Character orthogonality gives sum_{chi mod q}|M_chi(X)|^2=phi(q)sum_r|M_r|^2. ENT is therefore equivalent at every-epsilon exponent level to all fixed-q bounds |M_chi(X)|<<X^(1-c+epsilon).
quantitative_returns.joint_divergence: The full divergence from independent uniform sign and Haar residue is exactly J_X+D(P_R||Haar). The elementary bound is at most log 2+O_q(X^(-1)); the parity term may remain of order one.
quantitative_returns.ordinary_return: Under ENT, normal Abel continuation of s integral_1^infinity M_chi(x)x^(-s-1)dx gives 1/L(s,chi) and excludes regular zeros in Re(s)>1-c, with the principal pole handled as a reciprocal zero.
quantitative_returns.paid_residues: N_r=(X/q)C_q+O_q(sqrt X), C_q=product_{p not dividing q}(1-p^(-2))>0. Thus S=(phi(q)/q)C_q X+O_q(sqrt X) and p_r=1/phi(q)+O_q(X^(-1/2)). D(P_R||Haar)=O_q(X^(-1)), including marginal and CRT dependence costs.

This discharges only the fixed-parent main radical-size prerequisite.

hypotheses.full_bill: psi=Gamma_prime/Gamma. Let z_jp=eta_j(p)p^(-s_j), B_j=delta_j Re(1/s_j+1/(s_j-1))+(1/2)log(f_j/pi)+(1/2)Re psi((s_j+e_j)/2), E_j=sum_(p|q,p not|f_j)log p Re[z_jp/(1-z_jp)], C_j=B_j-E_j, Z_j=sum_rho (sigma-Re rho)/|s_j-rho|^2. quantitative_returns.differentiated_repair: With P fixed, Q_P=-partial_sigma S_P=sum Lambda(n)log n n^-sigma P(theta_n)=-C_Pprime+Z_Pprime>=0. Remove precisely one target copy from j=1. Then a1/(sigma-beta)^2<=-C_Pprime+sum_Rest a_j[(jt-Im rho)^2-(sigma-Re rho)^2]/|s_j-rho|^4. The complete absolutely summable Rest retains other target copies, all shifts and all far zeros, whose derivative contributions can be positive.
quantitative_returns.explicit_derivatives: B_jprime=delta_j Re[-1/s_j^2-1/(s_j-1)^2]+(1/4)Re psi_prime((s_j+e_j)/2); E_jprime=-sum_removed(log p)^2 Re[z_jp/(1-z_jp)^2], C_jprime=B_jprime-E_jprime. Constant log conductors disappear; gamma, local-factor and pole costs remain.

Since C0>0 and C0+C2>=0, a strict certificate exists iff R>0 and R^2>C0(C0+C2)/2, with b_opt=R/C0; strict real choices admit rational approximants.

statement:
## G3 — p<.10, multiplicative/noncommutative dual sector certificate

### W40-11 — Conditional expectation with a paid off-diagonal return; p=.08
O: Split a multiplicative operator into a conditional-expectation block and its complement, retaining the off-diagonal blocks rather than applying a triangle inequality.
B: A full block dual certificate or Schur complement might let a rigorously bounded structured sector pay for its entire complement.
T: For a 2 by 2 self-adjoint block matrix derive the exact minimum complement price as a function of the cross block.
X: The cross block can saturate the whole target norm; sector savings alone do not transfer.
R: Reusable exact criterion for when a restricted result can improve a full-form exponent.

### W40-12 — Multiplicative matrix martingale with signed increments; p=.06
O: Reveal prime valuations successively and encode coefficients as matrix martingale differences so that prime-local mean-zero identities survive noncommuting projections.
B: A variance bound plus explicit predictable drift could control the full signed moment more sharply than summing divisor patterns.
T: Two-prime model with noncommuting projectors; compute the drift created by revealing shifted arguments.
X: Arithmetic dependence and projector nonadaptedness may make drift as large as the original moment.
R: High upstream reach if drift has arithmetic cancellation; exact no-go if it cannot.

### W40-13 — Free-compression dimension diagnostic; p=.03
O: Compare a sector projector and arithmetic covariance projector through principal angles, using free-probability behavior only as a diagnostic, never as an assumption.
B: A deterministic principal-angle lower bound could make the restricted/complement interaction contractive.
T: Construct two rank-half projections with the same traces but arbitrary principal angles and test whether trace data give any uniform saving.
X: Dimension or equidistribution alone does not imply angle control; arithmetic projectors may align.
R: Precise obstruction to an attractive toy heuristic, redirecting work to an explicit angle statistic.

### W40-14 — Noncommutative sector capacity dual; p=.025
O: Define the smallest diagonal/block majorant of the actual signed full operator under a fixed sector budget, and write its semidefinite dual as a flow of test matrices.
B: A low-cost explicit dual witness or primal majorant could certify the exact complement price uniformly in size.
T: Solve an arrowhead block example with one structured sector and two interacting complements; compare separate versus joint complement payment.
X: Optimizing a finite matrix gives no arithmetic uniformity, and the full operator may be inaccessible.
R: Exact variational target capable of combining weak sector estimates without silently dropping cross terms.

### W40-15 — GNS positivity failure as a detector redesign; p=.012
O: Attempt to realize the signed arithmetic correlation functional as a positive state on a multiplicative algebra; use its negative Gram direction to construct a correction.
B: A bounded correction turning it into a positive state might unlock noncommutative moment bounds while preserving the zero implication.
T: Compute the smallest Gram minor on two prime generators with a signed coefficient and determine the exact positivity defect.
X: A positive correction may erase precisely the arithmetic cancellation; no bounded correction may exist.
R: A rigorous obstruction or a new corrected detector, not a license to assume positivity.

quantitative_returns.exact_deflation: a_W=a*product_(p in P)(delta1+chi(p)delta_p); A_W(s)=[L(2s,chi^2)/L(s,chi)] product_(p in P)(1+chi(p)p^-s). The finite multiplier has no zero for Re s>0. F_W(x)=sum_(d|W)chi(d)F_a(x/d), and F_a(x)=sum_(n P-smooth)a(n)F_W(x/n). Complete small shifted scales and the infinite smooth tail are retained by absolute damping.
quantitative_returns.positive_mass: At exponent gamma>0 the inverse coefficient mass is product_(p in P)(1-p^-gamma)^-1. For0<gamma<1 and P containing only unramified primes<=Y, it is <=exp(C_gamma Y^(1-gamma)). At gamma=3/4, Y=log^(4-delta)X with fixed0<delta<4 gives X^o(1). This is a coefficient price, not a bound on F_W. Controlled uniform small-scale decay can pay the far shifted tail; constants for the remaining same-bank source bounds must be explicit.
quantitative_returns.positive_orbit: product_(j=0)^(h-1)L(s,chi^j)=product_(p not dividing q)(1-p^(-r_p s))^(-h/r_p), Re s>1. Coefficients are nonnegative and the principal pole remains. Positivity on the real absolute-convergence ray does not exclude complex zeros. Conjugation sends a zero at rho to a conjugate-character zero at conjugate rho, not generally the same rho.
quantitative_returns.sharp_extreme: If W is exactly the product of unramified primes<=Y with Y>sqrt(X), then sum_(n<=X)a_W(n)=1-sum_(Y<p<=X,p not dividing q)chi(p). This changed-source identity provides no lower bound for the original sum.

hypotheses.cap: For the subpower corollaries assume N(rad H)<=C_H Z^E, with fixed E>=0 and fixed C_H before Z>=2 and all moving characters, masks and heights. G285/G286 provide only their own admitted caps; no reduced-conductor substitution is licensed.
hypotheses.normalization: For b=0,1 define P_chi^b(W,D;sigma,omega)=D^(-1/2) sum_{I!=0} mu(I)^b C_chi(I) W(NI/D)(NI/D)^(-sigma+i omega). b=1 means mu*chi, not inversion of chi. Every norm phase uses the positive real argument shown.
hypotheses.objects: Work over the Eisenstein integer ring O. H is a nonzero ideal, J=rad(H), N is ideal norm, and C_chi is the source completely multiplicative ideal coefficient, zero at the zero ideal and |C_chi(I)|<=1. mu is ideal Mobius. W is bounded measurable and supported in fixed [A,B], 0<A<B. D>0, sigma lies in a fixed compact real interval and omega is real. Character puncturing has coefficient e_H(I)C_chi(I), e_H(I)=1_{(I,H)=1}. Write chi_H=excluded(chi,H), P_H=P_chi_H.
hypotheses.raw_data: RawMoment(data,W,c,kappa_raw,C) means: for every Hrow>=1,D>0 with D^(1+c)<=Hrow and every finite set of nonzero element rows u with N((u))<=Hrow, sum_u |P_(data.character u)^1(W,D;0,0)|^2<=C*Hrow*(Hrow*max(1,D))^kappa_raw. Require c,kappa_raw,C>=0 and the literal RowData structure (eta,m,f), m,f nonzero with the original lambda|m and 2|m gates.

quantifier_scope.fixed_data: W,sigma,omega are fixed in each log-scale coordinate. beta>0, theta in (0,beta), annulus, parent and norm exponents precede the scale. Constants may depend on these fixed data and epsilon, but not on moving H,D or heights. No uniform constant is asserted as beta tends to 0.
quantifier_scope.raw_mask: For RM fix H before the rows and scales. Form data_H=(excluded eta H,m,f); all-ideal coefficient equality follows from the exact RowData/rowTwist identity. Every needed log, twist or scale profile variant retains its own original RawMoment premise. No bound on an arbitrary opaque character presentation is inferred.
quantifier_scope.weighted_rows: Finite-prefix bounds may be squared and summed with any fixed nonnegative row weights for varying H_l under one uniform cap and fixed profile/height data in each coordinate. This does not turn a restricted-scale arithmetic bank into a prefix bank.

quantitative_returns.convolutions: P_H^0(W,D)=sum_{d|J} mu(d)C_chi(d)/sqrt(Nd)*P_chi^0(W,D/Nd). P_H^1(W,D)=sum_{d H-smooth} C_chi(d)/sqrt(Nd)*P_chi^1(W,D/Nd); terms Nd>B*D vanish. All smooth powers are retained in the inverse sum; no extra sigma/omega divisor power occurs.
quantitative_returns.global_transform: Only when the input lies in the weighted L2 space may the global operator estimate be applied. The trivial actual bound P=O(sqrt D) ensures global integrability and an absolutely convergent transform on beta>1. On that line Fourier[e^(-kappa_log x)f_b](xi)=S_chi^b(beta+i xi)*M_W(beta-sigma+i(xi+omega)), where S_chi^b(s)=sum_{I!=0}mu(I)^b C_chi(I)(NI)^(-s) and M_W(z)=integral_0^infinity W(t)t^(z-1)dt. No continuation past reciprocal-L poles is supplied; xi is dual scale frequency, not the original omega.
quantitative_returns.operator: Put x=log D, f_b(x)=P_chi^b(W,e^x), S_h f(x)=f(x-h), c_P=C_chi(P) and A_H=product_{P|H}(Id-c_P NP^(-1/2)S_log(NP)). Then f_H,0=A_H f_0 and f_H,1=A_H^(-1)f_1. Restoring plain uses A_H^(-1), while restoring mu uses A_H. For beta=1/2+kappa_log>0, Fourier(F)(xi)=integral F(x)e^(-i xi x)dx, the conjugated multiplier is E_H(beta+i xi)=product_P(1-c_P NP^(-beta-i xi)). Both operator norms are <=K_beta(H)=product_P(1-NP^(-beta))^(-1); under the cap K_beta<=C_(beta,epsilon) Z^epsilon for every fixed epsilon>0.
quantitative_returns.prefix: Let ell=-log B, R_X=1_{x<=X}, F_b=e^(-kappa_log x)f_b. Since f_b=0 for x<ell and all delays are nonnegative, R_X A=R_X A R_X and likewise for A^(-1). Thus ||R_X F_H,b||_2<=K_beta||R_X F_b||_2, and conversely, for every finite X. Both sides are finite.
quantitative_returns.raw_transfer: RawMoment(data_H,W,c,kappa_raw,C*K_(1/2)(H)^2) follows. Weighted Cauchy in the H-smooth expansion costs K_(1/2)^2. For D'=D/Nd>0, D'^(1+c)<=D^(1+c)<=Hrow and max(1,D')<=max(1,D), so the original premise covers every shifted row sum, including D'<1. The coefficients C_(data.character u)(d) may vary with u but have modulus at most 1. Under the cap this is a named arbitrary-epsilon fee.
quantitative_returns.window: For I=[L,X], V>=1 and 0<theta<beta: ||1_I F_H,b||_2<=K_beta||1_[L-log V,X]F_b||_2 + V^(-theta)K_(beta-theta)||1_[ell,X]F_b||_2; the reverse bound holds too. Earlier scales and the tail are actual costs. For inverseProfile(V0,W,Dstar,D)(t)=V0(D*t/Dstar)W(t), joint shifts with v>=1, (Dstar,D)->(Dstar/v,D/v) retain the exact profile, but can cross the required Dstar>=U (tstar>=1) boundary.

raw_source_record.statement: Finite Euler deletion acts by a causal, invertible delay operator on the normalized ideal detector. Its weighted log-scale L2 norm and inverse are bounded by K_beta(H) for fixed beta>0. This gives exact finite-prefix transfer and a finite-window estimate with explicit earlier-scale leakage. For one fixed mask it also transfers the actual RawMoment premise at constant C*K_(1/2)(H)^2, including all shifted scales below 1. It does not control a partition into arbitrarily many moving masks or supply an arithmetic moment.

hypotheses.detector: Use the exact polynomial P_chi^b(W,D;sigma,omega)=D^(-1/2)sum_{I!=0}mu(I)^b C_chi(I)W(NI/D)(NI/D)^(-sigma+i omega), b=0,1. C_chi is completely multiplicative and bounded by1. Both detector factors share the SAME selected chi_l and H_l, with a common sigma,omega when applying Q. The actual cutoff has norm<=1 and positiveAnnular is fixed smooth with support [1/4,9/4]. Write A=1/4, B=Bann=9/4.
hypotheses.finite_setup: Over the Eisenstein ring, N is ideal norm, e_H(I)=1_{(I,H)=1}, omega(I) counts distinct prime divisors and tau(I) counts ideal divisors. L is a finite row/packet set, S a finite set of nonzero ideals, a:S->C, K_l:S->C and w_l>=0. Define T a(l)=sum_{I in S}a(I)K_l(I). For each squarefree ideal d define a_d(I)=1_{d|I}a(I). The arithmetic premise Q is sum_l w_l|T a_d(l)|^2<=B_Q sum_I|a_d(I)|^2 for EVERY such d, with ONE B_Q>=0 and the actual projected norm. A bound for all complex arrays on S suffices but is not necessary.
hypotheses.subpower: Fix N(rad H_l)<=C_H Z^E uniformly in l and max_{I in S}NI<=C_S Z^L0, with fixed C_H,C_S,E,L0 before Z and the rows. Fixed degree, annulus, source parents and ray data do not grow with Z.
hypotheses.uniformity: The same premise is required for each actual coefficient/profile/height fiber used in the conclusion, including the derivative arrays in the optional height transfer. A prescribed smooth-profile estimate, an unweighted count or G270 alone does not imply Q.

quantifier_scope.choice_order: Fix U=Z^d, d in a fixed compact positive interval, common tstar and base/ray/profile data before choosing row witnesses. Then fix a dyadic length fiber and, for the pointwise estimate, sigma,omega. Q uses the original fixed physical weights. Row-dependent profiles or labels must remain in the kernel bank or receive a proved uniform payment.
quantifier_scope.native_application: The admitted error dictionary of G287, when invoked, uses H=upsilon.modulus*(R*C)*Qprime^k*E2, u_err=p^(2*m_err)*jointSourceRow, (k,m_err)=(1,1),(6,0),(7,1), Qprime=(p). Both first reflections, E2=C2/D2, right signed -z, inverse right ray, physical outer conjugation and all WholeSourceIndex labels remain. Only the strengthened existential source selector has this dictionary; opaque norm/energy-only choices are not upgraded.
quantifier_scope.witness: Keep the same masked character, chosen zero rho, selected whole-family upper bins, dyadic indices, both spikes and inverseProfile. The theorem transfers only the upper moment. It does not create an unmasked witness or a new natural zero.

quantitative_returns.DP: Let M=max({1} union {2^omega(H_l):l in L}) and R=max({1} union {2^omega(I):I in S}). Then sum_l w_l|sum_I a(I)K_l(I)e_H_l(I)|^2<=M*B_Q*sum_I 2^omega(I)|a(I)|^2<=M*R*B_Q*sum_I|a(I)|^2. Inclusion-exclusion gives sum_{d|rad H_l}mu(d)T a_d(l); Cauchy costs M, discarding the nonnegative row restriction d|H_l permits Q, and summing d counts the squarefree divisors of each I. No I=dJ substitution, rescaling or distinct-mask count occurs.
quantitative_returns.coefficient_norm: NK<=Bann^2 Di Dp and sum_K|a(K)|^2<=max_{NK<=Bann^2 Di Dp}tau(K)*(sum_I|ai(I)|^2)*(sum_J|ap(J)|^2). Fixed annuli, compact sigma range, the actual bounded inverseProfile and Eisenstein O(Y+1) lattice counting bound each separate slot norm by a constant; when a term exists Bann*D>=1 absorbs +1. Hence the composite norm is subpower at fixed polynomial scales. Fixed further common-character slots use d_k and retain their literal coefficients and norm costs; their common-row dictionary must be established.
quantitative_returns.composite: Put Di=U^r, Dp=U^m, Wi(t)=cutoff(Di*t/U^tstar)*positiveAnnular(t), Wp=positiveAnnular. Set ai(I)=Di^(-1/2)mu(I)Wi(NI/Di)(NI/Di)^(-sigma+i omega), ap(J)=Dp^(-1/2)Wp(NJ/Dp)(NJ/Dp)^(-sigma+i omega), a(K)=sum_{IJ=K}ai(I)ap(J). Then P_chi_H^1(Wi,Di)P_chi_H^0(Wp,Dp)=sum_K a(K)C_chi(K)e_H(K). Overlapping I,J and squareful K are retained, with no coprimality assumption. The full norm phase is (NK/(Di*Dp))^(-sigma+i omega).
quantitative_returns.divisor_cost: For every fixed delta>0, 2^omega(I)<=tau(I)<=C_delta(NI)^delta; the same subpower estimate holds for fixed-degree divisor functions d_k. Thus MR<=C_epsilon Z^epsilon under the displayed fixed polynomial caps. The loss consumes a named epsilon allowance, not an arithmetic gain.
quantitative_returns.heights: Let F_l be the masked composite polynomial above and K0 a fixed compact sigma interval. For a fixed common profile/length fiber, derivatives in omega and sigma multiply composite coefficients by i*log(NK/(Di*Dp)) and -log(NK/(Di*Dp)), respectively; these logs lie in [2 log A,2 log B]. If Q is uniform for the arrays and their mixed first derivatives on a fixed enlarged compact sigma interval, successive local Sobolev inequalities give sum_l w_l sup_{sigma in K0,|omega|<=Omega}|F_l(sigma,omega)|^2<=C*(1+Omega)*B_Q*Z^epsilon. Use Omega=2*pi*allowance+3*i*T for the witness. This positive height cost is not epsilon. A degree-J arithmetic height bound instead pays degree J+1; an already supplied source reproducer is paid once, not duplicated.
quantitative_returns.lengths: Here .51<a0<=1 is the zero threshold. The preserved source constraints are 1<=tstar<=3/2, tstar-1/2-76*epsilon<=r<=tstar+epsilon, 0<=m<=1/2+75*epsilon, r+m>=tstar-epsilon, U^r=2^left and U^m=2^right. Sigma=Re rho in [.51,1], omega=2*pi*nu-Im rho, |nu|<=allowance, |Im rho|<=3*i*T; each original spike is at least U^((a0-1/2)*length-epsilon). The row mask stays inside the original witness.
quantitative_returns.native_costs: G286 caps are 12/9 for all admitted allocations with original P_j>=1/nonzero frozen first coefficients, and 11/8 for k=6; Qprime^6 remains. Retain 16*(k+1)*localErrorCost, one56/#P, localErrorCost=NQprime^(-1) for k=1,7 and (1-NQprime^(-1))^2 for k=6, volume/(rho_raw*NQprime^k), raw-frequency exponent q+2*m_err*a_prime, all allocations and independent height tails. Passing raw rows to FreeRow still needs its exact weighted sixth-power fiber. M_w(x)=sum_{l:Phi(l)=x}w_l must use the original weights; with varying selected subsets keep wtilde_l=w_l Z^[delta(p_l+z_Jl)-g(q,z_Jl)].

hypotheses.finite_setup: Over the Eisenstein ring, N is ideal norm, e_H(I)=1_{(I,H)=1}, omega(I) counts distinct prime divisors and tau(I) counts ideal divisors. L is a finite row/packet set, S a finite set of nonzero ideals, a:S->C, K_l:S->C and w_l>=0. Define T a(l)=sum_{I in S}a(I)K_l(I). For each squarefree ideal d define a_d(I)=1_{d|I}a(I). The arithmetic premise Q is sum_l w_l|T a_d(l)|^2<=B_Q sum_I|a_d(I)|^2 for EVERY such d, with ONE B_Q>=0 and the actual projected norm. A bound for all complex arrays on S suffices but is not necessary.
hypotheses.subpower: Fix N(rad H_l)<=C_H Z^E uniformly in l and max_{I in S}NI<=C_S Z^L0, with fixed C_H,C_S,E,L0 before Z and the rows. Fixed degree, annulus, source parents and ray data do not grow with Z.
hypotheses.uniformity: The same premise is required for each actual coefficient/profile/height fiber used in the conclusion, including the derivative arrays in the optional height transfer. A prescribed smooth-profile estimate, an unweighted count or G270 alone does not imply Q.

quantitative_returns.DP: Let M=max({1} union {2^omega(H_l):l in L}) and R=max({1} union {2^omega(I):I in S}). Then sum_l w_l|sum_I a(I)K_l(I)e_H_l(I)|^2<=M*B_Q*sum_I 2^omega(I)|a(I)|^2<=M*R*B_Q*sum_I|a(I)|^2. Inclusion-exclusion gives sum_{d|rad H_l}mu(d)T a_d(l); Cauchy costs M, discarding the nonnegative row restriction d|H_l permits Q, and summing d counts the squarefree divisors of each I. No I=dJ substitution, rescaling or distinct-mask count occurs.
quantitative_returns.coefficient_norm: NK<=Bann^2 Di Dp and sum_K|a(K)|^2<=max_{NK<=Bann^2 Di Dp}tau(K)*(sum_I|ai(I)|^2)*(sum_J|ap(J)|^2). Fixed annuli, compact sigma range, the actual bounded inverseProfile and Eisenstein O(Y+1) lattice counting bound each separate slot norm by a constant; when a term exists Bann*D>=1 absorbs +1. Hence the composite norm is subpower at fixed polynomial scales. Fixed further common-character slots use d_k and retain their literal coefficients and norm costs; their common-row dictionary must be established.
quantitative_returns.composite: Put Di=U^r, Dp=U^m, Wi(t)=cutoff(Di*t/U^tstar)*positiveAnnular(t), Wp=positiveAnnular. Set ai(I)=Di^(-1/2)mu(I)Wi(NI/Di)(NI/Di)^(-sigma+i omega), ap(J)=Dp^(-1/2)Wp(NJ/Dp)(NJ/Dp)^(-sigma+i omega), a(K)=sum_{IJ=K}ai(I)ap(J). Then P_chi_H^1(Wi,Di)P_chi_H^0(Wp,Dp)=sum_K a(K)C_chi(K)e_H(K). quantitative_returns.divisor_cost: For every fixed delta>0, 2^omega(I)<=tau(I)<=C_delta(NI)^delta; the same subpower estimate holds for fixed-degree divisor functions d_k. quantitative_returns.heights: Let F_l be the masked composite polynomial above and K0 a fixed compact sigma interval. For a fixed common profile/length fiber, derivatives in omega and sigma multiply composite coefficients by i*log(NK/(Di*Dp)) and -log(NK/(Di*Dp)), respectively; these logs lie in [2 log A,2 log B]. If Q is uniform for the arrays and their mixed first derivatives on a fixed enlarged compact sigma interval, successive local Sobolev inequalities give sum_l w_l sup_{sigma in K0,|omega|<=Omega}|F_l(sigma,omega)|^2<=C*(1+Omega)*B_Q*Z^epsilon. Use Omega=2*pi*allowance+3*i*T for the witness. This positive height cost is not epsilon. A degree-J arithmetic height bound instead pays degree J+1; an already supplied source reproducer is paid once, not duplicated.

quantitative_returns.CRT: e_H is idempotent with zeros, hence has no pointwise multiplicative inverse on a deleted nonzero coefficient. For two masks e1+e2-e1*e2=1-(1-e1)(1-e2); the omitted sector meets both masks. Distinct primes P|H1,Q|H2 with surviving chi coefficients give the literal squarefree blind ideal I=P*Q, mu(I)=+1 and C_chi(I)!=0. A common surviving P gives I=P, mu(I)=-1. These affect a particular detector only when its actual profile support includes their norms. Redundant masks killing only already-zero coefficients have no such obstruction. CRT reconstructs residues, not amplitudes deleted by both masks.
quantitative_returns.additive: On O/P define a_P(1)=1-1/q_P and a_P(xi)=-1/q_P for each nontrivial xi. Then 1_{a!=0}=sum_xi a_P(xi)xi(a). Set a_J(xi)=product_P a_P(xi_P). For I=(alpha)!=0 let Phi_xi(I)=(1/6)sum_{u in O^units}xi(u*alpha mod J). Unit averaging makes Phi independent of alpha and |Phi|<=1. Exactly e_H(I)=1_{(I,H)=1}=sum_xi a_J(xi)Phi_xi(I).
quantitative_returns.conductor: Define J_xi as the product of P for which xi_P is nontrivial. For theta>=0, sum_xi|a_J(xi)|N(J_xi)^theta=product_P(1-1/q_P)(1+q_P^theta). For theta>0 this equals NJ^theta product_P(1-1/q_P)(1+q_P^(-theta)). All full-conductor phases together already have l1 mass product_P(1-1/q_P). Unit averaging preserves the local nontrivial support and licenses no erasure of level cost. A moment loss N(J_xi)^theta safely costs Z^(E*theta+epsilon), not merely Z^epsilon.
quantitative_returns.mass: Lambda(J)=sum_xi|a_J(xi)|=product_{P|J}2(1-1/q_P)<=2^omega(J)<=C_epsilon Z^epsilon. The number of phases is NJ, which can be polynomial. |P_H^b|^2<=Lambda sum_xi|a_J(xi)||P_(chi;Phi_xi)^b|^2. For the simultaneous product, |P_H^1 P_H^0|^2<=Lambda^2 sum_{xi,eta}|a_J(xi)a_J(eta)||P_(chi;Phi_xi)^1 P_(chi;Phi_eta)^0|^2. The pushed positive weight has total extra mass Lambda^4; individual phase-tested spikes can lose Lambda and require a named allowance.
quantitative_returns.pair_level: Under the normalized measure |a_J(xi)a_J(eta)|/Lambda^2, each local component is trivial with probability1/2 independently for xi and eta. Thus P divides lcm(J_xi,J_eta) with probability3/4, and the exact normalized level moment is product_{P|J}[(1+3*q_P^theta)/4]. Include the Lambda^4 Cauchy mass when applying this to the product energy; separate conductor losses use the product of the one-phase masses.
quantitative_returns.polynomial: Let P_(chi;Phi)^b insert Phi(I) into the literal detector coefficient. Then P_chi_H^b(W,D;sigma,omega)=sum_xi a_J(xi)P_(chi;Phi_xi)^b(W,D;sigma,omega), with no change of D, W, normalization or phase. Physical conjugation conjugates Phi; it is not the Mobius bool.
quantitative_returns.signs: For P|J set s_P(I)=1-2*1_{P|I}. Then e_H(I)=2^(-omega(J))sum_{S subset primeSupport(J)}product_{P in S}s_P(I). This positive expansion has 2^omega(J) subpower many sign functions and l1 mass1. It holds on all prime-power patterns, but s_P(P^2)=-1 while s_P(P)^2=1, so these are not completely multiplicative characters. The inverse polynomial discards nonsquarefree inputs through mu; the plain polynomial does not.

Q=delta_1-p chi(p)delta_p, R_j=delta_1-p^(-j)delta_p, P=Q^J product_(0<=j<K)R_j, b=P*chi. In particular R_j has no chi(p) in its second coefficient. b is bounded mean-zero periodic of period dividing qp^(J+K); L_b=P L is entire and L_b(-j)=0 for j<K.

T_(X,W)(x)=sum_(a_1,...,a_5<=U; product a_i>D) product_i m(a_i) sum_(n_1,...,n_4>=1)product_j b(n_j) sigma_W((product a_i)(product n_j)) w((product a_i)(product n_j)/x). Q=delta_1-p chi(p)delta_p, R_j=delta_1-p^(-j)delta_p, P=Q^J product_(0<=j<K)R_j, b=P*chi. T_(X,W)(x)=sum_(a_1,...,a_5<=U; product a_i>D) product_i m(a_i) sum_(n_1,...,n_4>=1)product_j b(n_j) sigma_W((product a_i)(product n_j)) w((product a_i)(product n_j)/x). All factors are ordered, shared primes allowed, and the joint product edge is literal.
hypotheses.profile_cuts: Fix integer r>=4K+12 and w(y)=(1-y)^r on[0,1], zero above1. On every real shell X<=x<=2X, X>=2, freeze U=(2X)^(1/5). Set D=X^(1-delta), sigma_W(n)=product_(ell|W)(1-1_(ell^2|n)). W=1 is allowed.

statement:
## G4 — p<.10, analytic continuation/control representation replacement

### W40-16 — Hankel realization before moment formation; p=.075
O: Interpret a smoothed Dirichlet series as a Hankel operator on height or log-scale inputs; use a finite-dimensional realization only after proving a norm-controlled projection.
B: A low-rank approximation with a rigorously bounded residual could turn zero exclusion into a small determinant estimate.
T: A single delayed impulse has low sampled rank but high continuous Hankel rank; compute the aliasing counterexample.
X: Sampling or finite truncation may destroy the zero location, and small Hankel rank need not be uniform.
R: High ceiling architecture change; exact counterexample can rule out an unjustified numerical shortcut.

### W40-17 — Passive realization obstruction; p=.04
O: Ask whether an analytically continued logarithmic derivative admits a passive positive-real transfer realization after explicit subtractions.
B: Passivity would give a boundary-to-interior coercive inequality that detects an off-line zero.
T: One-zero rational example; calculate the Hermitian part in the target half-plane with and without a subtraction.
X: Positive-realness may be equivalent to the desired zero-free result, hence circular.
R: Precise circularity diagnosis or a new arithmetic sufficient condition for passivity.

### W40-18 — Compressed-shift defect detector; p=.035
O: Place a completed/mollified L-function in a Hardy-space model and use the compressed multiplication operator's defect vector as the zero witness.
B: A arithmetic upper bound on the defect resolvent could exclude the eigenvalue corresponding to a forbidden zero.
T: Blaschke single-zero model; compute defect norm and show whether it remembers distance from the boundary quantitatively.
X: Factorization may assume unavailable boundary norms or introduce a singular inner factor.
R: High ceiling, exact quantitative bridge needed from actual coefficients to a resolvent norm.

### W40-19 — Balanced truncation with a two-height error budget; p=.018
O: Treat the two-height kernel as input-output map and truncate modes according to controllability times observability rather than raw singular size.
B: A deterministic tail error paid in the original norm could preserve a zero signal while suppressing expensive modes.
T: A nonnormal 2 by 2 realization with small Hankel singular value but large transient response tests the correct norm.
X: Infinite-dimensional stability and actual detector norm may invalidate control-theory truncation bounds.
R: Constructive restricted numerical tool only after a complete analytic residual proof.

### W40-20 — Herglotz measure repair from negative mass; p=.006
O: Represent an analytically continued detector by a signed boundary measure and explicitly split its negative Jordan mass as an auxiliary state.
B: If arithmetic bounds make the negative mass subcritical, a positive Herglotz part could still enforce an interior exclusion margin.
T: Signed two-atom measure: derive the exact zero position versus negative mass and atom separation.
X: Tiny negative mass concentrated near a boundary point can place a zero arbitrarily close to the target; total variation may be insufficient.
R: Rare replacement architecture, with a cheap decisive concentration obstruction.
title: G4 — p<.10, analytic continuation/control representation replacement

## G5 — p<.01, far-gap H phase/projectors, geometry/discrete optimization

### W40-21 — Minimum-frustration forest certificate; p=.009
O: Build the exact ordered H incidence graph, choose a maximum-weight forest, gauge its phases away and pay every non-tree edge by its cycle holonomy.
B: An explicit graph energy identity could bound H by a flat part plus a computable frustration term while both arithmetic projectors remain attached.
T: Compare a triangle, a long cycle and a tree; determine whether large total curvature can yield a spectral saving without graph expansion.
X: Flat tree pieces can carry all mass, and large-girth graphs can have negligible normalized gap.
R: Constructive hard H attack with exact obstruction separating phase information from expansion requirements.

### W40-22 — Complex cone-cover certificate for ordered interactions; p=.007
O: Cover actual H edge phases by narrow cones chosen through a discrete partition; pair cones through exact projector-preserving involutions.
B: Opposed cones with nearly equal weighted masses could cancel before absolute estimates, leaving a provably small unmatched flow.
T: Solve the optimal transport balance for four phase atoms with unequal multiplicities and derive a total-variation residual.
X: Phase coverage does not imply matching masses; involutions may not preserve primes, shifts, gcd or height constraints.
R: Algorithmic certificate whose sole hard input is a full arithmetic imbalance bound.

### W40-23 — Discrete complex Laplacian domination; p=.005
O: Embed H in a magnetic connection Laplacian and seek a signed factorization H = D*D minus an explicitly bounded diagonal, with exact edge projectors.
B: A coercive lower bound for D*D could create the missing cancellation in H without termwise prime estimates.
T: Factor the three-cycle matrix and check the sign of the diagonal correction and both projection orders.
X: Positive Laplacian control often bounds the wrong side of H, or the correction restores the full trivial bound.
R: High-reach structural reformulation; exact sign failure would be a useful stop result.

### W40-24 — Integer cycle-flow cancellation; p=.008
O: Treat signed H incidences as a circulation and decompose balanced integer flows into cycles; attach the actual complex product to each cycle.
B: A bounded residual imbalance plus cancellation around short arithmetic cycles could control the whole signed packet.
T: Exact min-cost circulation on a small ordered multigraph, keeping repeated edges and zero coefficients, then derive the residual identity.
X: Additive complex edge sums do not telescope from multiplicative cycle holonomy; phase/coefficient compatibility is extra.
R: New exact full-return identity if compatibility holds; otherwise a sharp obstruction to graph-only reasoning.

### W40-25 — Determinant-line compatibility of two projectors; p=.003
O: Track the determinant line of the two arithmetic projector images along parameter shifts; use their relative phase as an invariant of otherwise incompatible local representations.
B: A nonzero winding or determinant separation could force an orthogonality defect across all bad profiles.
T: Two rank-one projections moved around a triangle: compute overlap products and show what is gauge-invariant versus norm-informative.
X: Berry phase may be nontrivial while all pairwise overlaps approach one; topological information alone has no power scale.
R: Very high ceiling only with quantitative metric control; likely useful conceptual obstruction.

## G6 — p<.01, sieve/information construction from obstruction

### W40-26 — Sieve syndrome with exact erasure completion; p=.009
O: Label each integer/prime configuration by its divisibility syndrome at selected small primes; use an error-correcting partition to retain separated syndromes and reconstruct omitted cells exactly.
B: An exact syndrome expansion with a small weighted erasure return might extend a restricted coprime-sector saving to the complete form.
T: Two-prime inclusion-exclusion table with signed coefficients and all repeated/gcd cases; derive the missing-cell price.
X: The erased syndrome may concentrate all difficult mass, and cardinality sparsity is not weighted norm sparsity.
R: Explicit full complementary return target, potentially useful for local exceptional sectors.

### W40-27 — Overlap cancellation as a Möbius code; p=.007
O: Treat overlapping sieve restrictions as parity-check equations on a Boolean lattice; Möbius inversion yields a signed reconstruction with coefficients chosen to cancel dominant overlap defects.
B: A short exact reconstruction could keep a useful restricted estimate while controlling its complement by lower-complexity overlaps.
T: Derive the three-restriction reconstruction and minimize the l1 reconstruction norm subject to exactness on every cell.
X: Exactness on the all-bad cell can force unit or larger complement weight, so no unconditional gain follows.
R: Exact identity and an optimization obstruction; possible gain only with a separately proved all-bad bound.

### W40-28 — Parity-homology cancellation of collision patterns; p=.004
O: Build a chain complex of repeated-prime collision patterns, with signed boundary maps encoding merging/splitting of indices.
B: Exact cancellation of boundary pairs could leave only a small homology sector, replacing a divisor-pattern count by a topological obstruction count.
T: Three-index collision lattice: write the boundary signs and test d squared equals zero against actual multiplicities.
X: Actual arithmetic coefficients need not respect the chosen incidence signs, so abstract homology may be unrelated.
R: Hard upstream route to connected-pattern cancellation; precise coefficient compatibility is the first gate.

### W40-29 — Phase list-decoding inequality; p=.006
O: Regard near-aligned arithmetic phases as codewords; list-decoding bounds would limit how many prime configurations can coherently reinforce any target phase.
B: A weighted cap on coherent lists at every phase and scale could directly power-save the complete ordered H sum.
T: Derive the exact relationship between a phase-arc concentration bound and the magnitude of the complex sum, including clustered antipodes.
X: A fixed arc occupancy bound below one is only a constant saving; a power saving needs scale-dependent discrepancy or cancellation.
R: New quantitative arithmetic target or proof that a coding analogy cannot deliver the missing exponent.

### W40-30 — CRT orthogonal-array detector; p=.008
O: Choose a family of local residue weights forming an orthogonal array, then combine them by CRT into a signed detector whose low-order collision projections vanish exactly.
B: Vanishing low-order correlations could lower the required full moment while a separately controlled high-order tail retains the zero signal.
T: Construct the smallest two-prime array and test its average against a fixed multiplicative character and its shifted copies.
X: Orthogonality may kill the fixed-character signal or require moduli growing too quickly for the transfer.
R: High ceiling replacement detector, with an explicit signal-versus-cancellation tradeoff.

End of initial seeds. No first-test outcomes have been computed or used in these cards.

statement:
## G67. Signed logarithmic bounds return the complete exponent

For f analytic near |z-t0|<=R, R>=16, f(t0)!=0, and any unit interval I
containing t0, let B>=sup_disk|f|. Avoid boundary zeros by varying R. Then

    integral_I log|f(t)|dt
      >=log|f(t0)|-(8/log R)log(B/|f(t0)|).

The proof uses the nonnegative superharmonic function
log(B/|f|), its positive harmonic part and the complete disk Green sum over
zeros with multiplicity. Near zeros have integrated Green excess at most4
and center Green value at least(log R)/2; far zeros and the harmonic part
obey the explicit Harnack bound. Real logarithmic singularities are integrable.
No zero separation, multiplicity cap or discarded negative logarithm is used.

For coefficients with sum|a_n|n^-b finite, the fixed Gaussian is entire and

    |F(z)| <= (2pi tau)^(-1/2)sum|a_n|n^-b
               exp(b Re z+tau b^2/2+(Im z)^2/(2tau)).

Choose t0 at a maximum on [j,j+1] and R in[sqrt j,2sqrt j]. Writing
M_j=max|F| and J_j=integral_j^(j+1)log|F| gives

    (1+eta_j)log M_j <= J_j+eta_j log B_j,
    eta_j=O(1/log j), log B_j=O(j).

Consequently J_j<=(gamma+epsilon)j+C_epsilon on EVERY sufficiently large
integer interval, for every epsilon>0, is equivalent in exponent to the
complete pointwise bound and the complete all-shell L2 bound. Jensen proves
the moment-to-log direction; the Green comparison returns the maximum with
only O(j/log j) loss. Sparse intervals or an average over j do not suffice.
This settles W21-T29's missing nonconcentration question for this complete
Gaussian class. It does not defeat the old smooth-signal or exceptional-dyad
counterexamples under their different hypotheses.

The actual Mellin numerator is

    integral_R F_chi(u)e^(-su)du=exp(tau s^2/2) N_chi(s)H_chi(s)/L(s,chi),
    N_chi=1-2chi(2)2^-s,
    H_2=(1-z_2)^-2, H_3=(1-z_3)^-2,
    H_p=(1-2z_p)/(1-z_p)^2 (p>=5), z_p=chi(p)p^-s.

H and its inverse converge absolutely for each fixed Re(s)>1/2. The finite
N zeros lie on Re(s)=1, or N=1 when2 is ramified. Full left Gaussian tails
and the improved right tail give continuation; multiplication by L excludes
zeros in gamma<Re(s)<1 without assuming reciprocal growth. The principal
pole and the known right boundary remain separate. A first gain needs
gamma<.874861; gamma=5/6 or3/4 gives the respective conditional targets.

The author also proves a finite upper certificate, preserving both zeros
and tails. For N>=exp(j+1), put

    T_(N,j)=exp(j+1+tau/2)barPhi((log N-j-1-tau)/sqrt tau).

With T>=T_(N,j)>0, an explicit derivative bound K_j, M midpoint samples v_k
and absolute errors delta_k,

    J_j <= M^-1 sum_k log(|v_k|+delta_k+T)+K_j/(4MT).

All parameters and sufficient asymptotic cutoff/sample budgets are in
author L8-L10 and critic Q8. This is a finite certificate for inspected
intervals. Its success on every large interval remains OPEN. Finite
quadrature ancestry includes G63; no new numerical evidence is promoted.
title: G67. Signed logarithmic bounds return the complete exponent

## G68. Exact degree energy and the retained arithmetic response

Let P contain2 and exclude3, Q=product P, q_p=1/p, and
a_P(n)=product_(p in P)(1-2*1_(p|n)). Set r_P=f3 a_P so that
f3=a_P r_P and r_P(pn)=r_P(n) for every p in P and every power. Under the
exact product reference law, Z_p=(B_p-q_p)/sqrt(q_p(1-q_p)). The expansion

    a_P=sum_S A_S Z_S,
    A_S=(-1)^|S| product_(p in S)2sqrt(q_p(1-q_p))
                      product_(p notin S)(1-2q_p)

has degree-energy polynomial

    sum_S A_S^2 z^|S|=product_p[(1-nu_p)+nu_p z],
    nu_p=4(p-1)/p^2.

Thus the discarded squared norm rho_D^2 is exactly Pr(K>D) for an
auxiliary Poisson-binomial ENERGY variable. It is not a random model of
arithmetic phases. nu_2=1 forces every nonzero term to contain2.

For the full Gaussian integer law, the existing W41/G54 CRT theorem gives
L1 error epsilon_X=O_A(X^-A) when Q<=X^(1-delta), delta>0 fixed.
The truncated polynomial q_D has |q_D|<=sqrt Q, so the complete error is

    |F_chi-F_(P,D,chi)| <= Z(u)[rho_D+2sqrt(Q epsilon_X)],
    Z(u)=sum_n g_tau(log n-u)~exp(tau/2)e^u.

Its literal realization, with D_pV(u)=V(u-log p), is
